:ś atha catuś catvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
vāsudevādipratimālakṣaṇavidhiḥ
43.d:
शिलां कृत्वा पिण्डिकार्थं किञ्चिन्न्यूनान्तु कल्पयेत् /
रथे स्थाप्य समानीय सवस्त्रां कारुवेश्मनि /
पूजयित्वाथ घटयेत् प्रतिमां स तु कर्मकृत् //
:ए इत्य् आदि महापुराणे आग्नेये शान्त्यादिवर्णनं नाम
त्रिचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुश् चत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
वासुदेवादिप्रतिमालक्षणविधिः
43.m:
Having fashioned the stone, he should design [another] slightly smaller for the pedestal. / Placing it on a chariot, bringing it covered with cloth to the artisan's workshop, / and worshipping it, that workman should fashion the image.
Thus ends the forty-third chapter, entitled “Description of Rites for Pacification and Image-stone Selection”, in the great and venerable Agni Purāṇa.
Now, chapter forty-four:
The rules on the characteristics of the images of Vāsudeva and other deities.

44.s:
bhagavānuvāca
vāsudevādipratimālakṣaṇaṃ pravadāmi te /
prāsādasyottare pūrvamukhīṃ vā cottarānanāṃ //
44.d:
भगवानुवाच
वासुदेवादिप्रतिमालक्षणं प्रवदामि ते /
प्रासादस्योत्तरे पूर्वमुखीं वा चोत्तराननां //
44.m: The Blessed Lord said: / I shall tell you the characteristics of the image of Vāsudeva and others. / To the north of the temple, [having placed the stone] facing east or facing north,

44.s:
saṃsthāpya pūjya ca baliṃ datvātho madhyasūcakaṃ /
śilāṃ śilpī tu navadhā vibhajya navame 'ṃśake //
44.d:
संस्थाप्य पूज्य च बलिं दत्वाथो मध्यसूचकं /
शिलां शिल्पी तु नवधा विभज्य नवमे ऽंशके //
44.m: having installed it, worshipped it, and given an oblation indicating the centre, / the artisan, dividing the stone into nine parts, in the ninth part,

44.s:
sūrpabhaktaiḥ śilāyāṃ tu bhāgaṃ svāṅgulamucyate /
dvyaṅgulaṃ golakaṃ nāmnā kālanetraṃ taducyate //
44.d:
सूर्पभक्तैः शिलायां तु भागं स्वाङ्गुलमुच्यते /
द्व्यङ्गुलं गोलकं नाम्ना कालनेत्रं तदुच्यते //
44.m: by measures of a grain of barley upon the stone, a part is called one's own digit (aṅgula); / two digits by name is a golaka; it is [also] called a kālanetra.

44.s:
bhāgamekaṃ tridhā bhaktvā pārṣṇibhāgaṃ prakalpayet /
bhāgamekaṃ tathā jānau grīvāyāṃ bhāgameva ca //
44.d:
भागमेकं त्रिधा भक्त्वा पार्ष्णिभागं प्रकल्पयेत् /
भागमेकं तथा जानौ ग्रीवायां भागमेव च //
44.m: Dividing one part into three, one should design the heel part; / likewise, one part for the knee, and one part for the neck.

44.s:
mukuṭaṃ tālamātraṃ syāttālamātraṃ tayā mukhaṃ /
tālenaikena kaṇṭhantu tālena hṛdayaṃ tathā //
44.d:
मुकुटं तालमात्रं स्यात्तालमात्रं तया मुखं /
तालेनैकेन कण्ठन्तु तालेन हृदयं तथा //
44.m: The crown should be a span (tāla) in measure, and the face a span in measure; / the throat is one span, and the chest is likewise a span;

44.s:
nābhimeḍhrāntarantālaṃ dvitālāvūrukau tathā /
tāladvayena jaṅghā syāt sūtrāṇi śṛṇu sāmprataṃ //
44.d:
नाभिमेढ्रान्तरन्तालं द्वितालावूरुकौ तथा /
तालद्वयेन जङ्घा स्यात् सूत्राणि शृणु साम्प्रतं //
44.m: the distance between the navel and the penis is a span, and the two thighs are two spans; / the lower leg should be two spans. Now listen to the plumb-lines.

44.s:
kāryaṃ sūtradvayaṃ pāde jaṅghāmadhye tathāparaṃ /
jānau sūtradvayaṃ kāryamūrūmadhye tathāparaṃ //
44.d:
कार्यं सूत्रद्वयं पादे जङ्घामध्ये तथापरं /
जानौ सूत्रद्वयं कार्यमूरूमध्ये तथापरं //
44.m: Two lines are to be made on the foot, and another in the middle of the lower leg; / two lines are to be made on the knee, and another in the middle of the thighs;

44.s:
meḍhre tathāparaṃ kāryaṃ kaṭyāṃ sūtrantathāparaṃ /
mekhalābandhasiddhyarthaṃ nābhyāṃ caivāparantathā //
:p 128
44.d:
मेढ्रे तथापरं कार्यं कट्यां सूत्रन्तथापरं /
मेखलाबन्धसिद्ध्यर्थं नाभ्यां चैवापरन्तथा //
:प् 128
44.m:
another is to be made at the penis, and another line at the waist; / and another at the navel to establish the fastening of the girdle;
[Page 128]

44.s:
hṛdaye ca tathā kāryaṃ kaṇṭhe sūtradvayaṃ tathā /
lalāte cāparaṃ kāryaṃ mastake ca tathāparaṃ //
44.d:
हृदये च तथा कार्यं कण्ठे सूत्रद्वयं तथा /
ललाते चापरं कार्यं मस्तके च तथापरं //
44.m: and likewise [a line] is to be made at the heart, and two lines at the neck; / another is to be made at the forehead, and another at the head;

44.s:
mukuṭopari kartavyaṃ sūtramekaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ /
sūtrāṇyūrdhvaṃ pradeyāni saptaiva kamalodbhava(1) //
44.d:
मुकुटोपरि कर्तव्यं सूत्रमेकं विचक्षणैः /
सूत्राण्यूर्ध्वं प्रदेयानि सप्तैव कमलोद्भव(1) //
44.m: one line should be made above the crown by the discerning. / Only seven vertical lines should be applied, O Lotus-Born One (Brahmā);

44.s:
kakṣātrikāntareṇaiva ghaṭ sūtrāṇi pradāpayet /
madhyasūtraṃ tu santyajya sūtrāṇyeva nivedayet //
44.d:
कक्षात्रिकान्तरेणैव घट् सूत्राणि प्रदापयेत् /
मध्यसूत्रं तु सन्त्यज्य सूत्राण्येव निवेदयेत् //
44.m: six lines should be placed across the armpits and hips. / Discarding the central line, one should lay down the other lines.

44.s:
lalāṭaṃ nāsikāvaktraṃ kartavyañcaturaṅgulaṃ /
grīvākarṇau tu kartavyau āyāmāccaturaṅgulau //
44.d:
ललाटं नासिकावक्त्रं कर्तव्यञ्चतुरङ्गुलं /
ग्रीवाकर्णौ तु कर्तव्यौ आयामाच्चतुरङ्गुलौ //
44.m: The forehead, nose, and mouth should be made four digits [each]; / the neck and ears should be made four digits in length;

44.s:
dvyaṅgule hanuke kārye vistārāccibukantathā /
aṣṭāṅgulaṃ lalāṭantu vistāreṇa prakīrtitam //
44.d:
द्व्यङ्गुले हनुके कार्ये विस्ताराच्चिबुकन्तथा /
अष्टाङ्गुलं ललाटन्तु विस्तारेण प्रकीर्तितम् //
44.m: the two jaws should be made two digits, and likewise the chin in width; / the forehead is declared to be eight digits in width;

44.s:
pareṇa dvyaṅgulau śaṅkhau kartavyāvalakānvitau /
caturaṅgulamākhyātamantaraṃ karṇanetrayoḥ //
44.d:
परेण द्व्यङ्गुलौ शङ्खौ कर्तव्यावलकान्वितौ /
चतुरङ्गुलमाख्यातमन्तरं कर्णनेत्रयोः //
44.m: further, the temples should be made two digits, accompanied by locks of hair; / the distance between the ear and the eye is declared to be four digits;

44.s:
dvyaṅgulau pṛthukau karṇau karṇāpāṅgārdhapañcame /
bhrūsamena tu sūtreṇa karṇaśrotraṃ prakīrtitam //
44.d:
द्व्यङ्गुलौ पृथुकौ कर्णौ कर्णापाङ्गार्धपञ्चमे /
भ्रूसमेन तु सूत्रेण कर्णश्रोत्रं प्रकीर्तितम् //
44.m: the two ears should be two digits wide, five and a half digits from the ear to the outer corner of the eye; / the ear-cavity is declared to be along the line level with the eyebrow;

44.s:
viddhaṃ ṣaḍaṅgulaṃ karṇamaviddhañcaturaṅgulam /
civukena samaṃ viddhamaviddhaṃ vā ṣaḍaṅgulam //
44.d:
विद्धं षडङ्गुलं कर्णमविद्धञ्चतुरङ्गुलम् /
चिवुकेन समं विद्धमविद्धं वा षडङ्गुलम् //
44.m: a pierced ear is six digits, and an unpierced one four digits; / pierced it may be level with the chin, or unpierced it may be six digits;

44.s:
gandhapātraṃ tathāvartaṃ śaṣkulīṃ kalpayettathā /
dvyaṅgulenādharaḥ kāryastasyārdhenottarādharaḥ //
44.d:
गन्धपात्रं तथावर्तं शष्कुलीं कल्पयेत्तथा /
द्व्यङ्गुलेनाधरः कार्यस्तस्यार्धेनोत्तराधरः //
44.m: one should fashion the concha, the helix, and the lobe of the ear. / The lower lip should be made two digits, and the upper lip half of that.

44.s:
ardhāṅgulaṃ tathā netraṃ(2) vaktrantu caturaṅgulam /
āyāmena tu vaipulyāt sārdhamaṅgulamucyate //
44.d:
अर्धाङ्गुलं तथा नेत्रं(2) वक्त्रन्तु चतुरङ्गुलम् /
आयामेन तु वैपुल्यात् सार्धमङ्गुलमुच्यते //
44.m: The eye is half a digit, and the mouth is four digits [in length]; / in width, however, it is stated to be one and a half digits.

44.s:
avyāttamevaṃ syādvaktraṃ vyāttaṃ tryaṅgulamiṣyate /
nāsāvaṃśasamucchrāyaṃ mūle tvekāṅgulaṃ matam //
44.d:
अव्यात्तमेवं स्याद्वक्त्रं व्यात्तं त्र्यङ्गुलमिष्यते /
नासावंशसमुच्छ्रायं मूले त्वेकाङ्गुलं मतम् //
44.m: Thus the mouth should be when closed; when open, it is prescribed as three digits. / The height of the nasal bridge is considered one digit at the base;

44.s:
ucchrāyā dvyaṅgulaṃ cāgre karavīropamāḥ smṛtāḥ /
:n
1 mukuṭopari iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 tathā gojī iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 129
antaraṃ cakṣuṣoḥ kāryaṃ caturaṅgulamānataḥ //
44.d:
उच्छ्राया द्व्यङ्गुलं चाग्रे करवीरोपमाः स्मृताः /
:न्
1 मुकुटोपरि इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 तथा गोजी इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 129
अन्तरं चक्षुषोः कार्यं चतुरङ्गुलमानतः //
44.m:
its height at the tip is two digits, and [the nostrils] are considered like oleander flowers.
:n
1 'Above the crown' is the reading in manuscript kha.
2 'Likewise the philtrum' is the reading in manuscript kha.
:p 132
The distance between the two eyes should be made four digits in measure.

44.s:
dvyaṅgulaṃ cākṣikoṇaṃ ca dvyaṅgulaṃ cāntaraṃ tayoḥ /
tārā netratribhāgeṇa dṛktārā pañcamāṃśikā //
44.d:
द्व्यङ्गुलं चाक्षिकोणं च द्व्यङ्गुलं चान्तरं तयोः /
तारा नेत्रत्रिभागेण दृक्तारा पञ्चमांशिका //
44.m: The corner of the eye is two digits, and the space between them is two digits. / The iris is one-third of the eye, and the pupil is one-fifth.

44.s:
tryaṅgulaṃ netravistāraṃ droṇī cārdhāṅgulā matā /
tatsamāṇā bhruvorlekhā bhruvau caiva same mate //
44.d:
त्र्यङ्गुलं नेत्रविस्तारं द्रोणी चार्धाङ्गुला मता /
तत्समाणा भ्रुवोर्लेखा भ्रुवौ चैव समे मते //
44.m: The length of the eye is three digits, and the eye-socket is considered half a digit. / The eyebrow line is equal to that [length], and the two eyebrows are considered equal.

44.s:
bhrūmadhyaṃ dvyaṅgulaṃ kāryaṃ bhrūdairghyaṃ caturāṅgulam(1) /
ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulāyāmammastakasya tu veṣṭanam //
44.d:
भ्रूमध्यं द्व्यङ्गुलं कार्यं भ्रूदैर्घ्यं चतुराङ्गुलम्(1) /
षट्त्रिंशदङ्गुलायामम्मस्तकस्य तु वेष्टनम् //
44.m: The space between the eyebrows should be made two digits, and the length of the eyebrow four digits. / The circumference of the head is thirty-six digits in extent.

44.s:
mūrtīnāṃ keśavādīnāṃ dvātriṃśadveṣṭanaṃ bhavet /
pañcanetrā tvadhogrīvā vistārādveṣṭanaṃ punaḥ //
44.d:
मूर्तीनां केशवादीनां द्वात्रिंशद्वेष्टनं भवेत् /
पञ्चनेत्रा त्वधोग्रीवा विस्ताराद्वेष्टनं पुनः //
44.m: For icons of Keśava and others, the circumference should be thirty-two [digits]. / The lower neck is five digits in width, while its circumference

44.s:
triguṇantu bhavedūrdhvaṃ vistṛtāṣṭāṅgulaṃ punaḥ /
grīvātriguṇamāyāmaṃ grīvāvakṣontaraṃ bhavet //
44.d:
त्रिगुणन्तु भवेदूर्ध्वं विस्तृताष्टाङ्गुलं पुनः /
ग्रीवात्रिगुणमायामं ग्रीवावक्षोन्तरं भवेत् //
44.m: should be threefold; the upper [neck] is again eight digits broad. / The length of the neck should be three times [its width], and such should be the distance between the neck and the chest.

44.s:
skandhāvaṣṭāṅgulau kāryau trikalāvaṃśakau śubhau /
saptanetrau smṛtau bāhū prabāhū ṣoḍaśāṅgulau //
44.d:
स्कन्धावष्टाङ्गुलौ कार्यौ त्रिकलावंशकौ शुभौ /
सप्तनेत्रौ स्मृतौ बाहू प्रबाहू षोडशाङ्गुलौ //
44.m: The two shoulders should be made eight digits, and the two collarbones auspicious with three kalās. / The upper arms are taught as seven digits, and the forearms as sixteen digits.

44.s:
trikalau vistṛtau bāhū prabāhū cāpi tatsamau /
bāhudaṇḍordhvato jñeyaḥ pariṇāhaḥ kalā nava //
44.d:
त्रिकलौ विस्तृतौ बाहू प्रबाहू चापि तत्समौ /
बाहुदण्डोर्ध्वतो ज्ञेयः परिणाहः कला नव //
44.m: The two upper arms are three kalās broad, and the forearms are equal to them. / At the top of the shaft of the arm, the circumference is to be known as nine kalās.

44.s:
saptadaśāṅgulo madhye kūrpārordhe ca ṣoḍaśa /
kūrpārasya bhavennāhaḥ triguṇaḥ kamalodbhava //
44.d:
सप्तदशाङ्गुलो मध्ये कूर्पारोर्धे च षोडश /
कूर्पारस्य भवेन्नाहः त्रिगुणः कमलोद्भव //
44.m: It is seventeen digits in the middle, and sixteen digits above the elbow. / The circumference of the elbow is three times that, O Lotus-born [Brahmā]!

44.s:
nāhaḥ prabāhumadhye tu ṣoḍaśāṅgula ucyate /
agrahaste parīṇāho dvādaśāṅgula ucyate //
44.d:
नाहः प्रबाहुमध्ये तु षोडशाङ्गुल उच्यते /
अग्रहस्ते परीणाहो द्वादशाङ्गुल उच्यते //
44.m: The circumference in the middle of the forearm is said to be sixteen digits. / The circumference at the wrist is said to be twelve digits.

44.s:
vistareṇa karatalaṃ kīrtitaṃ tu ṣaḍaṅgulam /
dairghyaṃ saptāṅgulaṃ kāryaṃ madhyā pajcāṅgulā matā //
44.d:
विस्तरेण करतलं कीर्तितं तु षडङ्गुलम् /
दैर्घ्यं सप्ताङ्गुलं कार्यं मध्या पज्चाङ्गुला मता //
44.m: The palm of the hand is declared to be six digits in breadth; / the length should be made seven digits, and the middle finger is considered five digits.

44.s:
tarjanyanāmikā caiva tasmādardhāṅgulaṃ vinā /
kaniṣṭhāṅguṣṭhakau kāryau caturaṅgulasammitau //
:n
1 bhrūdairghyāccaturaṅgulā iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 130
44.d:
तर्जन्यनामिका चैव तस्मादर्धाङ्गुलं विना /
कनिष्ठाङ्गुष्ठकौ कार्यौ चतुरङ्गुलसम्मितौ //
:न्
1 भ्रूदैर्घ्याच्चतुरङ्गुला इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 130
44.m:
The forefinger and ring finger are less than that by half a digit. / The little finger and thumb should be made measuring four digits.
:n
1 'Four digits in length of the eyebrow' is the reading in manuscript ṅa.
:p 130

44.s:
dviparvoṅguṣṭhakaḥ kāryaḥ śeṣāgulyastriparvikāḥ /
sarvāsāṃ parvaṇordhena nakhamānaṃ vidhīyate //
44.d:
द्विपर्वोङ्गुष्ठकः कार्यः शेषागुल्यस्त्रिपर्विकाः /
सर्वासां पर्वणोर्धेन नखमानं विधीयते //
44.m: The thumb should be made with two phalanges; the remaining fingers have three phalanges. / The measure of the nail for all [fingers] is prescribed as half a phalanx.

44.s:
vakṣaso yat pramāṇantu jaṭharaṃ tatpramāṇataḥ /
aṅgulaikaṃ bhavennābhī vedhena ca pramāṇataḥ //
44.d:
वक्षसो यत् प्रमाणन्तु जठरं तत्प्रमाणतः /
अङ्गुलैकं भवेन्नाभी वेधेन च प्रमाणतः //
44.m: Whatever the measure of the chest is, the abdomen is of that same measure. / The navel should be one digit in depth and measurement.

44.s:
tato meḍhrāntaraṃ kāryaṃ tālamātraṃ pramāṇataḥ /
nābhimadhye prīṇāho dvicatvāriṃśadaṅgulaiḥ //
44.d:
ततो मेढ्रान्तरं कार्यं तालमात्रं प्रमाणतः /
नाभिमध्ये प्रीणाहो द्विचत्वारिंशदङ्गुलैः //
44.m: From there, the distance to the penis should be made one tāla in measure. / The circumference at the middle of the navel is forty-two digits.

44.s:
antaraṃ stanayoḥ kāryaṃ tālamātraṃ pramāṇataḥ /
civukau(1) yavamānau tu maṇḍalaṃ dvipadaṃ bhavet //
44.d:
अन्तरं स्तनयोः कार्यं तालमात्रं प्रमाणतः /
चिवुकौ(1) यवमानौ तु मण्डलं द्विपदं भवेत् //
44.m: The space between the breasts should be made one tāla in measure. / The nipples measure one barley-corn each, and their halo should be two digits.

44.s:
catuḥṣaṣṭyaṅgulaṃ kāryaṃ veṣṭanaṃ vakṣasaḥsphuṭam /
caturmukhañca tadadhoveṣṭanaṃ parikīrtitam //
44.d:
चतुःषष्ट्यङ्गुलं कार्यं वेष्टनं वक्षसःस्फुटम् /
चतुर्मुखञ्च तदधोवेष्टनं परिकीर्तितम् //
44.m: The circumference of the chest should clearly be made sixty-four digits. / Below that, the circumference is declared to be four mukhas.

44.s:
pariṇāhas tathā kaṭyā catuḥpañcāśadaṅgulaiḥ /
vistāraścorumūle tu procyate dvādaśaṅgulaḥ //
44.d:
परिणाहस् तथा कट्या चतुःपञ्चाशदङ्गुलैः /
विस्तारश्चोरुमूले तु प्रोच्यते द्वादशङ्गुलः //
44.m: Likewise, the circumference of the waist is fifty-four digits. / And the breadth at the base of the thigh is stated as twelve digits.

44.s:
tasmādabhyadhikaṃ madhye tato nimnataraṃ kramāt /
vistṛtāṣṭāṅgulaṃ jānutriguṇā pariṇāhataḥ //
44.d:
तस्मादभ्यधिकं मध्ये ततो निम्नतरं क्रमात् /
विस्तृताष्टाङ्गुलं जानुत्रिगुणा परिणाहतः //
44.m: Greater than that in the middle, and from there gradually tapering. / The knee is eight digits broad and threefold in circumference.

44.s:
jaṅghāmadhye tu vistāraḥ saptāṅgula udāhṛtaḥ /
triguṇā paridhiścāsya jaṅghāgraṃ pañcavistarāt //
44.d:
जङ्घामध्ये तु विस्तारः सप्ताङ्गुल उदाहृतः /
त्रिगुणा परिधिश्चास्य जङ्घाग्रं पञ्चविस्तरात् //
44.m: The width in the middle of the shin is declared to be seven digits, / and its circumference is threefold; the top of the shin is five [digits] in width.

44.s:
triguṇā paridhiścāsya pādau tālapramāṇakau /
āyāmādutthitau pādau caturaṅgulameva ca //
44.d:
त्रिगुणा परिधिश्चास्य पादौ तालप्रमाणकौ /
आयामादुत्थितौ पादौ चतुरङ्गुलमेव च //
44.m: Its circumference is threefold; the two feet measure one tāla. / The feet raised in height are four digits.

44.s:
gulphāt pūrvaṃ tu kartavyaṃ pramāṇāccaturaṅgulam /
trikalaṃ vistṛtau pādau tryaṅgulo guhyakaḥ smṛtaḥ //
44.d:
गुल्फात् पूर्वं तु कर्तव्यं प्रमाणाच्चतुरङ्गुलम् /
त्रिकलं विस्तृतौ पादौ त्र्यङ्गुलो गुह्यकः स्मृतः //
44.m: Before the ankle should be made four digits in measure. / The two feet are three kalās broad; the big toe is known to be three digits.

44.s:
pañcāṅgulastu nāhosya dīrghā tadvat pradeśinī /
aṣṭamāṣṭāṃśatonyūnaḥ śeṣāṅgulyaḥ krameṇa tu //
44.d:
पञ्चाङ्गुलस्तु नाहोस्य दीर्घा तद्वत् प्रदेशिनी /
अष्टमाष्टांशतोन्यूनः शेषाङ्गुल्यः क्रमेण तु //
44.m: Its circumference is five digits; the second toe is equally long. / Decreasing by one-eighth [of a digit] progressively are the remaining toes.

44.s:
sapādāṅgulamutsedhamaṅguṣṭasya prakīrtitaṃ /
yavonamaṅgulaṃ kāryamaṅguṣṭhasya nakhaṃ tathā //
:n
1 cūcukau iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 131
44.d:
सपादाङ्गुलमुत्सेधमङ्गुष्टस्य प्रकीर्तितं /
यवोनमङ्गुलं कार्यमङ्गुष्ठस्य नखं तथा //
:न्
1 चूचुकौ इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 131
44.m:
The height of the big toe is proclaimed as one and a quarter digits; / the nail of the big toe should be made one digit less a barley-corn.
:n
1 'The two nipples' is the reading in manuscript ṅa.
:p 131

44.s:
ardhāṅgulaṃ tathānyāsāṃ(1) kramān nyūnaṃ tu kārayet /
aṅgulau vṛṣaṇau kāryau meḍhraṃ tu caturaṅgulam //
44.d:
अर्धाङ्गुलं तथान्यासां(1) क्रमान् न्यूनं तु कारयेत् /
अङ्गुलौ वृषणौ कार्यौ मेढ्रं तु चतुरङ्गुलम् //
44.m: For the others, one should make it gradually decrease by half a digit. / The testicles should be made two digits, and the penis four digits.

44.s:
pariṇāhotra koṣāgraṃ kartavyañcaturaṅgulam /
ṣaḍaṅgulaparīṇāhau vṛṣaṇau parikīrtitau //
44.d:
परिणाहोत्र कोषाग्रं कर्तव्यञ्चतुरङ्गुलम् /
षडङ्गुलपरीणाहौ वृषणौ परिकीर्तितौ //
44.m: Here the tip of the scrotum should be made four digits in circumference. / The testicles are declared to have a circumference of six digits.

44.s:
pratimā bhūṣaṇāḍhyā syādetaduddeśalakṣaṇam /
anayaiva diśā kāryaṃ loke dṛṣṭvā tu lakṣaṇam //
44.d:
प्रतिमा भूषणाढ्या स्यादेतदुद्देशलक्षणम् /
अनयैव दिशा कार्यं लोके दृष्ट्वा तु लक्षणम् //
44.m: The image should be richly ornamented; this is the summary of characteristics. / In this very manner, having observed [the figures] in the world, the characteristics should be made.

44.s:
dakṣiṇe tu kare cakramadhastāt padmameva ca /
vāme śaṅkhaṃ gadādhastādvāsudevasya lakṣaṇāt //
44.d:
दक्षिणे तु करे चक्रमधस्तात् पद्ममेव च /
वामे शङ्खं गदाधस्ताद्वासुदेवस्य लक्षणात् //
44.m: In the right hand [is] the discus, and below it the lotus; / in the left [is] the conch, and below it the mace, according to the characteristics of Vāsudeva.

44.s:
śrīpuṣṭau vāpi kartavye padmavīṇākarānvite /
ūrumātrocchitāyāme mālāvidyādharau(2) tathā //
44.d:
श्रीपुष्टौ वापि कर्तव्ये पद्मवीणाकरान्विते /
ऊरुमात्रोच्छितायामे मालाविद्याधरौ(2) तथा //
44.m: Śrī and Puṣṭi should also be made, holding a lotus and a vīṇā in their hands, / their height and length measuring up to the thighs; likewise two garland-bearing Vidyādharas,

44.s:
prabhāmaṇḍalasaṃsthau tau prabhā hastyādibhūṣaṇā /
padmābhaṃ pādapīṭhantu pratimāsvevamācaret //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye pratimālakṣaṇaṃ nāma catuś
catvāriṃśodhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcacatvāriṃśodhyāyaḥ
piṇḍikālakṣaṇakathanaṃ
44.d:
प्रभामण्डलसंस्थौ तौ प्रभा हस्त्यादिभूषणा /
पद्माभं पादपीठन्तु प्रतिमास्वेवमाचरेत् //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये प्रतिमालक्षणं नाम चतुश्
चत्वारिंशोध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चचत्वारिंशोध्यायः
पिण्डिकालक्षणकथनं
44.m:
both situated on the halo, which is adorned with elephants and the like. / The footstool should resemble a lotus; thus should one make for images.
:e Thus in the Agnipurāṇa, the primeval Mahāpurāṇa, the forty-fourth chapter, named 'The Characteristics of Images' [is concluded].
:ś Now the forty-fifth chapter.
The Statement on the Characteristics of the Pedestal

45.s:
bhagavānuvāca
piṇḍikālakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye dairghyeṇa pratimāsamā /
ucchrāyaṃ pratimārdhantu catuḥṣaṣṭipuṭāṃ(2) ca tām //
45.d:
भगवानुवाच
पिण्डिकालक्षणं वक्ष्ये दैर्घ्येण प्रतिमासमा /
उच्छ्रायं प्रतिमार्धन्तु चतुःषष्टिपुटां(2) च ताम् //
45.m: The Blessed Lord said: / I shall state the characteristics of the pedestal: it is equal to the image in length, / and its height is half of the image; it is divided into sixty-four compartments.

45.s:
tyaktvā paṅktidvayaṃ cādhastadūrdhvaṃ yattu koṣṭhakam /
:n
1 sārdhāṅgulaṃ tathāyāmamiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 maṇividyādharāviti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 catuḥṣaṣṭipadāmiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 132
samantādubhayoḥ pārśve antasthaṃ parimārjayet //
45.d:
त्यक्त्वा पङ्क्तिद्वयं चाधस्तदूर्ध्वं यत्तु कोष्ठकम् /
:न्
1 सार्धाङ्गुलं तथायाममिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 मणिविद्याधराविति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 चतुःषष्टिपदामिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 132
समन्तादुभयोः पार्श्वे अन्तस्थं परिमार्जयेत् //
45.m:
Leaving two rows below, whatever square is above that,
:n
1 'Likewise one and a half digits in length' is the reading in manuscript ṅa.
2 'Jewel-bearing Vidyādharas' is the reading in manuscript gha.
3 'Consisting of sixty-four squares' is the reading in manuscript ṅa.
:p 132
on both sides all around, one should erase the interior [squares].

45.s:
ūrdhvaṃ paṅgktidvayaṃ tyaktvā adhastād yattu koṣṭhakam /
antaḥ sammārjayet yatnāt pārśvayorubhayoḥ samam //
45.d:
ऊर्ध्वं पङ्ग्क्तिद्वयं त्यक्त्वा अधस्ताद् यत्तु कोष्ठकम् /
अन्तः सम्मार्जयेत् यत्नात् पार्श्वयोरुभयोः समम् //
45.m: Leaving two rows above, whatever square is below, / one should carefully erase inside, equally on both sides.

45.s:
tayormadhyagatau tatra catuṣkau mārjayettataḥ /
caturdhā bhājayitvā tu ūrdhvapaṅktidvayaṃ budhaḥ //
45.d:
तयोर्मध्यगतौ तत्र चतुष्कौ मार्जयेत्ततः /
चतुर्धा भाजयित्वा तु ऊर्ध्वपङ्क्तिद्वयं बुधः //
45.m: Then, one should erase the four-square space situated between the two. / Having divided the upper two rows into four parts, the wise person

45.s:
mekhalā bhāgamātrā syāt khātaṃ tasyārdhamānataḥ /
bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ parityajya pārśvayorubhayoḥ samaṃ //
45.d:
मेखला भागमात्रा स्यात् खातं तस्यार्धमानतः /
भागं भागं परित्यज्य पार्श्वयोरुभयोः समं //
45.m: should make the girdle one part in size, and the cavity half of that in measure. / Having left one part each equally on both sides,

45.s:
datvā caikaṃ padaṃ vāhye pramāṇaṃ kārayed budhaḥ /
tribhāgeṇa ca bhāgasyāgre syāttoyavinirgamaḥ //
45.d:
दत्वा चैकं पदं वाह्ये प्रमाणं कारयेद् बुधः /
त्रिभागेण च भागस्याग्रे स्यात्तोयविनिर्गमः //
45.m: and having given one square on the outside, the wise person should make the measurement. / And at one-third of a part in front should be the water spout.

45.s:
nānāprakārabhedena bhadreyaṃ(1) piṇḍikā śubhā /
aṣṭatālā tu kartavyā devī lakṣmīstayā striyaḥ //
45.d:
नानाप्रकारभेदेन भद्रेयं(1) पिण्डिका शुभा /
अष्टताला तु कर्तव्या देवी लक्ष्मीस्तया स्त्रियः //
45.m: With various types of divisions, this auspicious pedestal is of the Bhadra type. / The goddess Lakṣmī and other female [deities] should be made measuring eight tālas.

45.s:
bhruvau yavādhike kārye yavahīnā tu nāsikā /
golakenādhikaṃ vaktramūrdhvaṃ tiryagvivarjitaṃ //
45.d:
भ्रुवौ यवाधिके कार्ये यवहीना तु नासिका /
गोलकेनाधिकं वक्त्रमूर्ध्वं तिर्यग्विवर्जितं //
45.m: The two eyebrows should be made larger by one barley-corn, but the nose smaller by one barley-corn. / The mouth is greater by the eyeball, devoid of upward or oblique [distortion].

45.s:
āyate nayane kārye tribhāgonair yavaistribhiḥ /
tadardhena tu vaipulyaṃ netrayoḥ parikalpayet //
45.d:
आयते नयने कार्ये त्रिभागोनैर् यवैस्त्रिभिः /
तदर्धेन तु वैपुल्यं नेत्रयोः परिकल्पयेत् //
45.m: The two eyes should be made elongated by three barley-corns minus a third; / and one should fix the width of the two eyes as half of that.

45.s:
karṇapāśo .dhikaḥ kāryaḥ sṛkkaṇīsamasūtrataḥ /
namraṃ kalāvihīnantu kuryādaṃśadvayaṃ tathā //
45.d:
कर्णपाशो .धिकः कार्यः सृक्कणीसमसूत्रतः /
नम्रं कलाविहीनन्तु कुर्यादंशद्वयं तथा //
45.m:
The earlobe should be made larger, on an even line with the corners of the mouth;
and one should make the two parts sloping down, reduced by a digit.

45.s:
grīvā sārdhakalā kāryā tadvistāropaśobhitā /
netraṃ vinā tu vistārau ūrū jānū ca piṇḍikā //
45.d:
ग्रीवा सार्धकला कार्या तद्विस्तारोपशोभिता /
नेत्रं विना तु विस्तारौ ऊरू जानू च पिण्डिका //
45.m: The neck should be made one and a half kalās [in height], adorned with a width [equal to] that. / Leaving aside the eyes, [such are] the widths; and [so are] the thighs, the knees, and the pedestal.

45.s:
aṅghripṛṣṭhau sphicau kaṭyāṃ yathābhāgaṃ prakalpayet /
saptāṃśonās tathāṅgulyo dīrghaṃ viṣkambhanāhataṃ //
45.d:
अङ्घ्रिपृष्ठौ स्फिचौ कट्यां यथाभागं प्रकल्पयेत् /
सप्तांशोनास् तथाङ्गुल्यो दीर्घं विष्कम्भनाहतं //
45.m: One should fashion the tops of the feet and the buttocks on the hip in their proper proportion. / Likewise, the fingers are reduced by a seventh part, long, struck [proportionately] by the diameter.

45.s:
netraikavarjitāyāmā jaṅghorū ca tathā kaṭiḥ /
madhyapārśvaṃ ca tadvṛttaṃ ghanaṃ pīnaṃ kucadvayaṃ //
:n
1 tatreyamiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 133
45.d:
नेत्रैकवर्जितायामा जङ्घोरू च तथा कटिः /
मध्यपार्श्वं च तद्वृत्तं घनं पीनं कुचद्वयं //
:न्
1 तत्रेयमिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 133
45.m:
The shanks, thighs, and likewise the waist have a length minus one eye[-measure]; / and the waist-side is rounded, and the pair of breasts is firm and plump.
[...]
[Alternative reading:] 'tatreyamiti' is the variant reading in the manuscript marked ṅa. / [Page 133]

45.s:
tālamātrau stanau karyau kaṭiḥ sārdhakalādhikā /
lakṣma śeṣaṃ purāvatsyāt dakṣiṇe cāmubujaṃ kare //
45.d:
तालमात्रौ स्तनौ कर्यौ कटिः सार्धकलाधिका /
लक्ष्म शेषं पुरावत्स्यात् दक्षिणे चामुबुजं करे //
45.m: The breasts should be made one tāla [in size]; the waist is greater by one and a half kalās. / The remaining characteristic should be as before, and in the right hand an aquatic lotus.

45.s:
vāme vittvaṃ striyau pārśve śubhe cāmarahastake /
dīrghaghoṇastu garuḍaś cakrāṅgādyānatho vade //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye piṇḍikālakṣmādilakṣaṇaṃ
nāma pañcacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha ṣaṭcatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
śālagrāmādimūrtilakṣaṇakathanaṃ
45.d:
वामे वित्त्वं स्त्रियौ पार्श्वे शुभे चामरहस्तके /
दीर्घघोणस्तु गरुडश् चक्राङ्गाद्यानथो वदे //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये पिण्डिकालक्ष्मादिलक्षणं
नाम पञ्चचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ षट्चत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
शालग्रामादिमूर्तिलक्षणकथनं
45.m:
On the left, [the emblem of] wealth; two auspicious women on the sides holding chowries in their hands. / But Garuḍa has a prominent beak. Now I shall declare [the icons] marked with the disc and others.
Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter, titled 'The Characteristics of the Pedestal and other Marks', in the venerable Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
Now the forty-sixth chapter.
Declaration of the characteristics of the icons such as the śālagrāma.

46.s:
bhagavānuvāca
śālagrāmādimūrteś ca vakṣyehaṃ bhuktimuktidāḥ /
vāsudevo 'sito dvāre śālagrāmadvicakrakaḥ //
46.d:
भगवानुवाच
शालग्रामादिमूर्तेश् च वक्ष्येहं भुक्तिमुक्तिदाः /
वासुदेवो ऽसितो द्वारे शालग्रामद्विचक्रकः //
46.m: The Lord said: / I shall declare the icons of the śālagrāma and others, which grant worldly enjoyment and liberation. / Vāsudeva is black, has two discs of the śālagrāma at the entrance.

46.s:
jñeyaḥ saṅkarṣaṇo lagnadvicakro rakta uttamaḥ /
sūkṣmacakro bahucchidraḥ pradyumno nīladīghavaḥ //
46.d:
ज्ञेयः सङ्कर्षणो लग्नद्विचक्रो रक्त उत्तमः /
सूक्ष्मचक्रो बहुच्छिद्रः प्रद्युम्नो नीलदीघवः //
46.m: Saṅkarṣaṇa is to be known as having two joined discs, red, and excellent. / Pradyumna has a minute disc, many apertures, and a long blue body.

46.s:
pīto niruddhaḥ padmāṅgo vartulo dvitrirekhavān /
kṛṣṇo nārāyaṇo nābhyunnataḥ śuṣiradīrghavān //
46.d:
पीतो निरुद्धः पद्माङ्गो वर्तुलो द्वित्रिरेखवान् /
कृष्णो नारायणो नाभ्युन्नतः शुषिरदीर्घवान् //
46.m: Aniruddha is yellow, marked with a lotus, round, and possessing two or three lines. / Nārāyaṇa is black, elevated at the navel, and having a long cavity.

46.s:
parameṣṭho sābjacakraḥ pṛṣṭhacchidrakaś ca(1) vindumān /
sthūlacakro 'sito viṣṇurmadhye rekhā gadākṛtiḥ //
46.d:
परमेष्ठो साब्जचक्रः पृष्ठच्छिद्रकश् च(1) विन्दुमान् /
स्थूलचक्रो ऽसितो विष्णुर्मध्ये रेखा गदाकृतिः //
46.m: Parameṣṭhin is endowed with a lotus and a disc, has an aperture at the back, and is marked with dots. / Viṣṇu has a thick disc, is black, and has a line in the middle shaped like a mace.

46.s:
nṛsiṃhaḥ kapikaḥ sthūlavakraḥ syāt pañcavindukaḥ /
varāhaḥ śaktiliṅgaḥ syāt taccakrau viṣamau sṛtau //
46.d:
नृसिंहः कपिकः स्थूलवक्रः स्यात् पञ्चविन्दुकः /
वराहः शक्तिलिङ्गः स्यात् तच्चक्रौ विषमौ सृतौ //
46.m: Nṛsiṃha is tawny, has a thick curved [line], and possesses five dots. / Varāha has the mark of a spear; his two discs are uneven and spread out.

46.s:
indranīlanibhaḥ sthūlastrirekhālāñchitaḥ śubhaḥ /
kūrmastathonnataḥ pṛṣṭhe vartulāvartako 'sitaḥ //
46.d:
इन्द्रनीलनिभः स्थूलस्त्रिरेखालाञ्छितः शुभः /
कूर्मस्तथोन्नतः पृष्ठे वर्तुलावर्तको ऽसितः //
46.m: He resembles a sapphire, is thick, marked with three lines, and auspicious. / Kūrma is likewise elevated on the back, has a circular spiral, and is black.

46.s:
hayagrīvoṅkuśāvārarekho nīlaḥ savindukaḥ /
:n
1 pṛthuśccchidraśceti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 134
vaikuṇṭhaḥ ekacakro 'bjī maṇibhiḥ puccharekhakaḥ //
46.d:
हयग्रीवोङ्कुशावाररेखो नीलः सविन्दुकः /
:न्
1 पृथुश्च्च्छिद्रश्चेति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 134
वैकुण्ठः एकचक्रो ऽब्जी मणिभिः पुच्छरेखकः //
46.m:
Hayagrīva has a line resembling an elephant-goad, is blue, and marked with dots.
[...]
[Alternative reading:] 'pṛthuśccchidraśceti' is the variant reading in the manuscript marked ṅa. / [Page 134]
Vaikuṇṭha has a single disc, is endowed with a lotus, and has a tail-line with gems.

46.s:
matsyo dīrghastrivinduḥ syāt kācavarṇastu pūritaḥ /
śrīdharo vanamālāṅkaḥ pañjarekhastu vartulaḥ //
46.d:
मत्स्यो दीर्घस्त्रिविन्दुः स्यात् काचवर्णस्तु पूरितः /
श्रीधरो वनमालाङ्कः पञ्जरेखस्तु वर्तुलः //
46.m: Matsya is long, has three dots, has the color of glass, and is plump. / Śrīdhara is marked with a garland of forest flowers, has five lines, and is round.

46.s:
vāmano vartulaścātihrasvo nīlaḥ savindukaḥ /
śyāmastrivikramo dakṣarekho vāmena vindukaḥ //
46.d:
वामनो वर्तुलश्चातिह्रस्वो नीलः सविन्दुकः /
श्यामस्त्रिविक्रमो दक्षरेखो वामेन विन्दुकः //
46.m: Vāmana is round, exceedingly short, blue, and marked with dots. / Trivikrama is dark, has a line on the right, and a dot on the left.

46.s:
ananto nāgabhogāṅgo naikābho naikamūrtimān /
sthūlo dāmodaro madhyacakro dvāḥsūkṣmavindukaḥ(1) //
46.d:
अनन्तो नागभोगाङ्गो नैकाभो नैकमूर्तिमान् /
स्थूलो दामोदरो मध्यचक्रो द्वाःसूक्ष्मविन्दुकः(1) //
46.m: Ananta has the body of a serpent's coils, manifold luster, and manifold forms. / Dāmodara is thick, has a central disc, and small dots at the entrance.

46.s:
sudarśanastvekacakro lakṣmīnārāyaṇo dvayāt /
tricakraścācyuto devastricakrako vā trivikramaḥ //
46.d:
सुदर्शनस्त्वेकचक्रो लक्ष्मीनारायणो द्वयात् /
त्रिचक्रश्चाच्युतो देवस्त्रिचक्रको वा त्रिविक्रमः //
46.m: Sudarśana has a single disc; Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa has two; / the god Acyuta has three discs, or Trivikrama has three discs.

46.s:
janārdanaś catuś cakro vāsudevaś ca pañcabhiḥ /
ṣaṭvakraś caiva pradyumnaḥ saṅkarṣaṇañca saptabhiḥ //
46.d:
जनार्दनश् चतुश् चक्रो वासुदेवश् च पञ्चभिः /
षट्वक्रश् चैव प्रद्युम्नः सङ्कर्षणञ्च सप्तभिः //
46.m: Janārdana has four discs, and Vāsudeva has five; / Pradyumna has six curved [lines], and Saṅkarṣaṇa has seven.

46.s:
puruṣottamoṣṭacakro navavyūho navāṅkitaḥ /
daśāvatāro daśabhirdaśaikenāniruddhakaḥ /
dvādaśātmā dvādaśabhirata ūrdhvamanantakaḥ //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye śālagrāmādimūrtilakṣaṇaṃ nāma
ṣaṭcatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha saptacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
śālagrāmādipūjākathanaṃ
46.d:
पुरुषोत्तमोष्टचक्रो नवव्यूहो नवाङ्कितः /
दशावतारो दशभिर्दशैकेनानिरुद्धकः /
द्वादशात्मा द्वादशभिरत ऊर्ध्वमनन्तकः //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये शालग्रामादिमूर्तिलक्षणं नाम
षट्चत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ सप्तचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
शालग्रामादिपूजाकथनं
46.m:
Puruṣottama has eight discs; Navavyūha is marked with nine; / Daśāvatāra has ten; Aniruddha has eleven; / Dvādaśātman has twelve; beyond this, [the icon] is Ananta.
Thus ends the forty-sixth chapter, titled 'The Characteristics of the Icons such as the Śālagrāma', in the venerable Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
Now the forty-seventh chapter.
Declaration of the worship of the śālagrāma and other [stones].

47.s:
bhagavānuvāca
śālagrāmādicakrāṅkapūjāḥ siddhyai vadāmi te /
trividhā syāddhareḥ pūjā kāmyākāmyobhayātmikā //
47.d:
भगवानुवाच
शालग्रामादिचक्राङ्कपूजाः सिद्ध्यै वदामि ते /
त्रिविधा स्याद्धरेः पूजा काम्याकाम्योभयात्मिका //
47.m: The Lord said: / I shall declare to you the worship of the [stones] marked with discs such as the śālagrāma, for attainment. / Worship of Hari is of three kinds: with desire, desireless, and consisting of both.

47.s:
mīnādīnāntu pañcānāṃ kāmyātho vobhayātmikā(2) /
:n
1 madhyacakrādhaḥ sūkṣmavinduka iti ṅa,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 kāmyārthevobhayātmaketi gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 135
varāhasya nṛsiṃhasya vāmanasya ca muktaye //
47.d:
मीनादीनान्तु पञ्चानां काम्याथो वोभयात्मिका(2) /
:न्
1 मध्यचक्राधः सूक्ष्मविन्दुक इति ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 काम्यार्थेवोभयात्मकेति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 135
वराहस्य नृसिंहस्य वामनस्य च मुक्तये //
47.m:
For the five beginning with the Fish, [it is] with desire, or consisting of both;
[...]
[Alternative reading:] 'madhyacakrādhaḥ sūkṣmavinduka iti' is the variant reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
[Alternative reading:] 'kāmyārthevobhayātmaketi' is the variant reading in the manuscript marked gha. / [Page 135]
for Varāha, Nṛsiṃha, and Vāmana, [it is] for liberation.

47.s:
cakrādīnāṃ trayāṇāntu śālagrāmārcanaṃ śṛṇu /
uttamā niṣphalā pūjā kaniṣṭhā saphalārcanā //
47.d:
चक्रादीनां त्रयाणान्तु शालग्रामार्चनं शृणु /
उत्तमा निष्फला पूजा कनिष्ठा सफलार्चना //
47.m: Listen to the worship of the śālagrāma and others of the three, beginning with the disc: / The highest worship is without [desire for] fruit; the lowest worship is [attended] with fruit.

47.s:
madhyamā mūrtipūjā syāccakrābje caturasrake /
praṇavaṃ hṛdi vinyasya ṣaḍaṅgaṅkaradehayoḥ //
47.d:
मध्यमा मूर्तिपूजा स्याच्चक्राब्जे चतुरस्रके /
प्रणवं हृदि विन्यस्य षडङ्गङ्करदेहयोः //
47.m: The middling is the worship of the icon on a four-sided [diagram] with a disc and a lotus. / Having deposited the praṇava in the heart, and the six limbs upon the hands and body,

47.s:
kṛtamudrātrayaś cakrād vahiḥ pūve guruṃ yajet /
āpye gaṇaṃ vāyave ca dhātāraṃ nairṛte yajet //
47.d:
कृतमुद्रात्रयश् चक्राद् वहिः पूवे गुरुं यजेत् /
आप्ये गणं वायवे च धातारं नैरृते यजेत् //
47.m: having made the three ritual gestures, one should worship the guru outside the disc in the east; / one should worship Gaṇa in the west, Dhātṛ in the north-west, and Nairṛta in the south-west;

47.s:
vidhātārañca kartāraṃ hartāraṃ dakṣasaumyayoḥ /
viśvaksenaṃ yajedīśe āgneye kṣetrapālakam //
47.d:
विधातारञ्च कर्तारं हर्तारं दक्षसौम्ययोः /
विश्वक्सेनं यजेदीशे आग्नेये क्षेत्रपालकम् //
47.m: Vidhātṛ and the Creator and the Destroyer in the south and north; / one should worship Viṣvaksena in the north-east, and the Kṣetrapāla in the south-east;

47.s:
ṛgādivedān prāgādau ādhārānantakaṃ bhuvaṃ /
pīṭhaṃ padmaṃ cārkacandravahnyākhyaṃ maṇḍalatrayaṃ //
47.d:
ऋगादिवेदान् प्रागादौ आधारानन्तकं भुवं /
पीठं पद्मं चार्कचन्द्रवह्न्याख्यं मण्डलत्रयं //
47.m: the Vedas beginning with the Ṛgveda in the east and the other [quarters]; the Support, Ananta, the earth, / the seat, the lotus, and the three maṇḍalas named Sun, Moon, and Fire;

47.s:
āsanaṃ dvādaśārṇena tatra sthāpya śilāṃ yajet /
astena ca samastena svavījena yajet kramāt //
47.d:
आसनं द्वादशार्णेन तत्र स्थाप्य शिलां यजेत् /
अस्तेन च समस्तेन स्ववीजेन यजेत् क्रमात् //
47.m: having placed the stone there on the seat with the twelve-syllable mantra, one should worship it. / One should worship it successively with the weapon[-mantra], with the complete [mantra], and with its own seed-syllable.

47.s:
pūrvādāvatha vedādyair gāyatrībhyāṃ jitādinā /
praṇavenārcayet pañcānmudrāstisraḥ pradarśayet //
47.d:
पूर्वादावथ वेदाद्यैर् गायत्रीभ्यां जितादिना /
प्रणवेनार्चयेत् पञ्चान्मुद्रास्तिस्रः प्रदर्शयेत् //
47.m: Then in the east and other [directions], with the Vedic [mantras] and others, with the two Gāyatrīs, with [the hymn] beginning with 'Jita', / and with the praṇava, one should worship afterwards; one should show the three ritual gestures.

47.s:
viśvaksenasya cakrasya kṣetrapālasya darśayet /
śālagrāmasya prathamā pūjārtho niṣphalocyate //
47.d:
विश्वक्सेनस्य चक्रस्य क्षेत्रपालस्य दर्शयेत् /
शालग्रामस्य प्रथमा पूजार्थो निष्फलोच्यते //
47.m: One should show [the gestures] of Viṣvaksena, of the disc, and of the Kṣetrapāla. / The first worship of the śālagrāma is said to be without [desire for] fruit.

47.s:
pūrvavat ṣoḍaśārañca sapadmaṃ maṇḍalaṃ likhet /
śaṅkhacakragadākhaḍgair gurvādyaṃ pūrvavadyajet(1) //
47.d:
पूर्ववत् षोडशारञ्च सपद्मं मण्डलं लिखेत् /
शङ्खचक्रगदाखड्गैर् गुर्वाद्यं पूर्ववद्यजेत्(1) //
47.m: As before, one should draw a sixteen-spoked maṇḍala with a lotus. / With conch, disc, mace, and sword, one should worship the guru and the others as before.

47.s:
pūrve saumye dhanurvāṇān vedādyair āsanaṃ dadet /
śilāṃ nyased dvādaśārṇaistṛtīyaṃ pūjanaṃ śṛṇu //
47.d:
पूर्वे सौम्ये धनुर्वाणान् वेदाद्यैर् आसनं ददेत् /
शिलां न्यसेद् द्वादशार्णैस्तृतीयं पूजनं शृणु //
47.m: In the east and the north, [one places] bow and arrows; one should offer a seat with the Vedic [mantras] and others. / One should deposit the stone with the twelve-syllable mantra. Listen to the third worship:

47.s:
aṣṭāramabjaṃ vilikhet gurvādyaṃ(2) pūrvavadyajayet /
:n
1 caturbhiḥ pūrvavadyajediti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 gandhādyair iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 136
aṣṭārṇenāsanaṃ datvā tenaiva ca śilāṃ nyaset /
pūjayeddaśadhā tena gāyatrībhyāṃ jitaṃ tathā(1) //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye śālagrāmādipūjākathanaṃ nāma
saptacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athāṣṭācatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
caturviṃśatimūrtistotrakathanaṃ
47.d:
अष्टारमब्जं विलिखेत् गुर्वाद्यं(2) पूर्ववद्यजयेत् /
:न्
1 चतुर्भिः पूर्ववद्यजेदिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 गन्धाद्यैर् इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 136
अष्टार्णेनासनं दत्वा तेनैव च शिलां न्यसेत् /
पूजयेद्दशधा तेन गायत्रीभ्यां जितं तथा(1) //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये शालग्रामादिपूजाकथनं नाम
सप्तचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथाष्टाचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
चतुर्विंशतिमूर्तिस्तोत्रकथनं
47.m:
One should draw an eight-petalled lotus and worship the guru and the others as before.
[...]
[Alternative reading:] 'caturbhiḥ pūrvavadyajediti' is the variant reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
[Alternative reading:] 'gandhādyair iti' is the variant reading in the manuscript marked ṅa. / [Page 136]
Having offered the seat with the eight-syllable mantra, one should deposit the stone with that very [mantra].
One should worship tenfold with that, with the two Gāyatrīs, and likewise [with the hymn] 'Jita'.
Thus ends the forty-seventh chapter, titled 'Declaration of the Worship of the Śālagrāma and Others', in the venerable Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
Now the forty-eighth chapter.
Declaration of the hymn of praise to the twenty-four icons.

48.s:
bhagavānuvāca
oṃrūpaḥ keśavaḥ padmaśaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ /
nārāyaṇaḥ śaṅkhapadmagadācakrī pradakṣiṇaṃ //
48.d:
भगवानुवाच
ओंरूपः केशवः पद्मशङ्खचक्रगदाधरः /
नारायणः शङ्खपद्मगदाचक्री प्रदक्षिणं //
48.m: The Lord said: / Keśava, whose form is the syllable Oṃ, bears the lotus, conch, disc, and mace. / Nārāyaṇa holds the conch, lotus, mace, and disc in circumambulatory order.

48.s:
tato gado mādhavoriśaṅkhapadmī namāmi taṃ /
cakrakaumodakīpadmaśaṅkhī govinda ūrjitaḥ //
48.d:
ततो गदो माधवोरिशङ्खपद्मी नमामि तं /
चक्रकौमोदकीपद्मशङ्खी गोविन्द ऊर्जितः //
48.m: Next, Mādhava holds the mace, disc, conch, and lotus; I bow to him. / Govinda, mighty, holds the disc, Kaumodakī, lotus, and conch.

48.s:
bhokṣadaḥ śrīgadī padmī śaṅkhī viṣṇuś ca cakradhṛk /
śaṅkhacakrābjagadinaṃ madhusūdanamāname //
48.d:
भोक्षदः श्रीगदी पद्मी शङ्खी विष्णुश् च चक्रधृक् /
शङ्खचक्राब्जगदिनं मधुसूदनमानमे //
48.m: Viṣṇu, the grantor of liberation, holds Śrī, mace, lotus, conch, and disc. / I bow to Madhusūdana, who holds the conch, disc, lotus, and mace.

48.s:
bhaktyā trivikramaḥ padmagadī cakrī ca śaṅkhyapi /
śaṅkhacakragadāpadmī vāmanaḥ pātu māṃ sadā //
48.d:
भक्त्या त्रिविक्रमः पद्मगदी चक्री च शङ्ख्यपि /
शङ्खचक्रगदापद्मी वामनः पातु मां सदा //
48.m:
With devotion, Trivikrama holds a lotus, mace, discus, and conch.
May Vāmana, holding a conch, discus, mace, and lotus, always protect me.

48.s:
gaditaḥ śrīdharaḥ padmī cakraśārṅgī ca śaṅkhyapi(2) /
hṛṣīkeśo gadācakrī padmī cakraśaṅkhī ca pātu naḥ //
48.d:
गदितः श्रीधरः पद्मी चक्रशार्ङ्गी च शङ्ख्यपि(2) /
हृषीकेशो गदाचक्री पद्मी चक्रशङ्खी च पातु नः //
48.m:
Śrīdhara is described as holding a lotus, discus, bow, and conch.
May Hṛṣīkeśa, holding a mace, discus, lotus, and conch, protect us.

48.s:
varadaḥ padmanābhastu śaṅkhābjārigadādharaḥ /
dāmodaraḥ padmaśaṅkhagadācakrī namāmi taṃ //
48.d:
वरदः पद्मनाभस्तु शङ्खाब्जारिगदाधरः /
दामोदरः पद्मशङ्खगदाचक्री नमामि तं //
48.m:
Padmanābha is the boon-giver, holding a conch, lotus, discus, and mace.
I bow to Dāmodara, who holds a lotus, conch, mace, and discus.

48.s:
tene gadī śaṅkhacakrī vāsudevobjabhṛjjagat /
saṅkarṣaṇo gadī śaṅkhī padmī cakrī ca pātu vaḥ //
:n
1 jitaṃ tata iti kha, ga, ṅa, cihnitapustakatrayapāṭhaḥ
2 cakrī gadyatha śaṅkhyapi iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 137
48.d:
तेने गदी शङ्खचक्री वासुदेवोब्जभृज्जगत् /
सङ्कर्षणो गदी शङ्खी पद्मी चक्री च पातु वः //
:न्
1 जितं तत इति ख, ग, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकत्रयपाठः
2 चक्री गद्यथ शङ्ख्यपि इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 137
48.m:
Vāsudeva, holding a mace, conch, discus, and lotus, pervaded the world.
May Saṅkarṣaṇa, holding a mace, conch, lotus, and discus, protect you all.
[...]
[Footnote 1: The reading in the three manuscripts marked kha, ga, and ṅa is 'jitaṃ tataḥ'.]
[Footnote 2: The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'cakrī gadyatha śaṅkhyapi'.] / [Page 137]

48.s:
gadī cakrī śaṅkhagadī (1) pradyumnaḥ padmabhṛt prabhuḥ /
aniruddhaś cakragadī śaṅkhī padmī ca pātu naḥ //
48.d:
गदी चक्री शङ्खगदी (1) प्रद्युम्नः पद्मभृत् प्रभुः /
अनिरुद्धश् चक्रगदी शङ्खी पद्मी च पातु नः //
48.m:
Lord Pradyumna holds a mace, discus, conch, and lotus.
May Aniruddha, holding a discus, mace, conch, and lotus, protect us.

48.s:
sureśoryabjaśaṅkhāḍhyaḥ śrīgadī puruṣottamaḥ /
adhokṣajaḥ padmagadī śaṅkhī cakrī ca pātu vaḥ //
48.d:
सुरेशोर्यब्जशङ्खाढ्यः श्रीगदी पुरुषोत्तमः /
अधोक्षजः पद्मगदी शङ्खी चक्री च पातु वः //
48.m:
Puruṣottama, lord of the gods, is endowed with a discus, lotus, conch, and mace.
May Adhokṣaja, holding a lotus, mace, conch, and discus, protect you all.

48.s:
devo nṛsiṃhaś cakrābjagadāśaṅkhī namāmi tam /
acyutaḥ śrīgadī padmī cakrī śaṅkhī ca pātu vaḥ //
48.d:
देवो नृसिंहश् चक्राब्जगदाशङ्खी नमामि तम् /
अच्युतः श्रीगदी पद्मी चक्री शङ्खी च पातु वः //
48.m:
The god Nṛsiṃha holds a discus, lotus, mace, and conch; I bow to him.
May Acyuta, holding Śrī, a mace, lotus, discus, and conch, protect you all.

48.s:
bālarūpī śaṅkhagadī upendraś cakrapadmyapi /
janārdanaḥ padmacakrī śaṅkhadhārī gadādharaḥ //
48.d:
बालरूपी शङ्खगदी उपेन्द्रश् चक्रपद्म्यपि /
जनार्दनः पद्मचक्री शङ्खधारी गदाधरः //
48.m:
Upendra has the form of a child, holding a conch, mace, discus, and lotus.
Janārdana holds a lotus, discus, conch, and mace.

48.s:
śaṅkhī padmī ca cakrī ca hariḥ kaumodakīdharaḥ /
kṛṣṇaḥ śaṅkhī gadī padmī cakrī me bhuktimuktidaḥ //
48.d:
शङ्खी पद्मी च चक्री च हरिः कौमोदकीधरः /
कृष्णः शङ्खी गदी पद्मी चक्री मे भुक्तिमुक्तिदः //
48.m:
Hari holds a conch, lotus, discus, and the Kaumodakī [mace].
Kṛṣṇa holds a conch, mace, lotus, and discus; he grants me worldly enjoyment and liberation.

Vāsudeva is the primary icon; from him arose Saṅkarṣaṇa.
From Saṅkarṣaṇa arose Pradyumna, and from Pradyumna, Aniruddha.

48.s:
keśavādiprabhedena aikaikasya tridhā kramāt /
dvādaśākṣarakaṃ stotraṃ caturviṃśatimūrtimat /
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi nirmalaḥ sarvamāpnuyāt //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye caturviṃśatimūrtistotraṃ nāma
aṣṭācatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athonapañcāśo 'dhyāyaḥ
matsyādilakṣaṇavarṇanaṃ
48.d:
केशवादिप्रभेदेन ऐकैकस्य त्रिधा क्रमात् /
द्वादशाक्षरकं स्तोत्रं चतुर्विंशतिमूर्तिमत् /
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि निर्मलः सर्वमाप्नुयात् //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये चतुर्विंशतिमूर्तिस्तोत्रं नाम
अष्टाचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथोनपञ्चाशो ऽध्यायः
मत्स्यादिलक्षणवर्णनं
48.m:
By division into Keśava and the rest, three-fold in sequence for each one:
whoever recites or listens to this hymn of twelve syllables embodying the twenty-four icons,
becomes stainless and attains everything.
Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter, called 'Hymn of the Twenty-Four Icons', in the venerable Agni Mahāpurāṇa.
Now begins the forty-ninth chapter.
Description of the characteristics of Matsya and other [incarnations].

49.s:
bhagavānuvāca
daśāvatāraṃ matsyādilakṣaṇaṃ pravadāmi te /
matsyākārastu matsyaḥ syāt kūrmaḥ kārmākṛlirbhavet //
:n
1 śaṅkhapadmī iti ga, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 138
49.d:
भगवानुवाच
दशावतारं मत्स्यादिलक्षणं प्रवदामि ते /
मत्स्याकारस्तु मत्स्यः स्यात् कूर्मः कार्माकृलिर्भवेत् //
:न्
1 शङ्खपद्मी इति ग, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 138
49.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
I shall tell you the characteristics of the ten incarnations, beginning with Matsya:
Matsya should have the form of a fish, and Kūrma should have the form of a tortoise.
[...]
[Footnote 1: The reading in the two manuscripts marked ga and ṅa is 'śaṅkhapadmī'.] / [Page 138]

49.s:
narāṅgo vātha kartavyo bhūvarāho gadādibhṛt /
dakṣiṇe vāmake śaṅkhaṃ lakṣmīrvā padmameva vā //
49.d:
नराङ्गो वाथ कर्तव्यो भूवराहो गदादिभृत् /
दक्षिणे वामके शङ्खं लक्ष्मीर्वा पद्ममेव वा //
49.m:
Or Bhūvarāha should be made with a human body, bearing a mace and other attributes:
in the right [hand], and in the left hand a conch, or Lakṣmī, or a lotus.

49.s:
śrīvāmakūrparasthā tu kṣmānantau caraṇānugau /
varāhasthāpanādrājyaṃ bhavābdhitaraṇaṃ bhavet //
49.d:
श्रीवामकूर्परस्था तु क्ष्मानन्तौ चरणानुगौ /
वराहस्थापनाद्राज्यं भवाब्धितरणं भवेत् //
49.m:
Śrī rests on his left elbow, and Earth and Ananta accompany his feet.
From establishing Varāha, one attains kingship and crossing over the ocean of worldly existence.

49.s:
narasiṃho vivṛttāsyo vāmorukṣatadānavaḥ(1) /
tadvakṣo dārayanmālī sphuraccakragadādharaḥ //
49.d:
नरसिंहो विवृत्तास्यो वामोरुक्षतदानवः(1) /
तद्वक्षो दारयन्माली स्फुरच्चक्रगदाधरः //
49.m:
Narasiṃha has a wide-open mouth, tearing apart the demon on his left thigh,
ripping open his chest, wearing a garland, and bearing a radiant discus and mace.

49.s:
chatrī daṇḍī vāmanaḥ syādathavā syāccaturbhujaḥ /
rāmaścāpeṣuhastaḥ syāt kaḍgī paraśunānvitaḥ //
49.d:
छत्री दण्डी वामनः स्यादथवा स्याच्चतुर्भुजः /
रामश्चापेषुहस्तः स्यात् कड्गी परशुनान्वितः //
49.m:
Vāmana should hold an umbrella and staff, or he may have four arms.
Rāma should have bow and arrow in hand, holding a sword and accompanied by an axe.

49.s:
rāmaścāpī śarī khaḍgī śaṅkhī vā dvibhujaḥ smṛtaḥ /
gadālāṅgaladhārī ca rāmo vātha caturbhujaḥ //
49.d:
रामश्चापी शरी खड्गी शङ्खी वा द्विभुजः स्मृतः /
गदालाङ्गलधारी च रामो वाथ चतुर्भुजः //
49.m:
Or Rāma is traditionally known with two arms, holding a bow, arrow, sword, or conch;
or Rāma has four arms, bearing a mace and a plough.

49.s:
vāmordhve lāṅgalaṃ dadyādadhaḥ śaṅkhaṃ suśobhanaṃ /
muṣalaṃ dakṣiṇordhve tu cakrañcādhaḥ suśobhanaṃ //
49.d:
वामोर्ध्वे लाङ्गलं दद्यादधः शङ्खं सुशोभनं /
मुषलं दक्षिणोर्ध्वे तु चक्रञ्चाधः सुशोभनं //
49.m:
One should place a plough in his upper left [hand], and a beautiful conch below;
a pestle in the upper right [hand], and a beautiful discus below.

49.s:
śāntātmā lambakarṇaś ca gaurāṅgaścāmbarāvṛtaḥ(2) /
ūrdhvapadmasthito buddho varadābhayadāyakaḥ //
49.d:
शान्तात्मा लम्बकर्णश् च गौराङ्गश्चाम्बरावृतः(2) /
ऊर्ध्वपद्मस्थितो बुद्धो वरदाभयदायकः //
49.m:
Buddha has a peaceful mind, long ears, fair limbs, and is draped in garments;
seated on an upright lotus, he grants boons and fearlessness.

49.s:
dhanustūṇānvitaḥ(3) kalkī mlecchotsādakaro dvijaḥ /
athavāśvasthitaḥ khaḍgī śaṅkhacakraśarānvitaḥ //
49.d:
धनुस्तूणान्वितः(3) कल्की म्लेच्छोत्सादकरो द्विजः /
अथवाश्वस्थितः खड्गी शङ्खचक्रशरान्वितः //
49.m:
Kalki is a twice-born holding a bow and quiver, destroying the barbarians;
or he is mounted on a horse, bearing a sword, conch, discus, and arrows.

49.s:
lakṣaṇaṃ vāsudevādinavakasya vadāmi te /
dakṣiṇordhve gadā vāme vāmordhve cakramuttamaṃ //
49.d:
लक्षणं वासुदेवादिनवकस्य वदामि ते /
दक्षिणोर्ध्वे गदा वामे वामोर्ध्वे चक्रमुत्तमं //
49.m:
I shall tell you the characteristics of the nine [deities] beginning with Vāsudeva:
In the upper right [hand] is a mace; in the left, in the upper left [hand], an excellent discus.

49.s:
brahmeśau pārśvagau nityaṃ vāsudevosti pūrvavat /
śaṅkhī sa varado vātha dvibhujo vā caturbhujaḥ //
49.d:
ब्रह्मेशौ पार्श्वगौ नित्यं वासुदेवोस्ति पूर्ववत् /
शङ्खी स वरदो वाथ द्विभुजो वा चतुर्भुजः //
49.m:
Brahmā and Śiva are constantly at his sides; Vāsudeva is as described before,
holding a conch, granting boons, with either two arms or four arms.

49.s:
lāṅgalī muṣalī rāmo gadāpadmadharaḥ smṛtaḥ /
:n
1 vāmoruhṛtadānava iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 gaurāṅgaścāyudhāvṛta iti kha, ga,
cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
3 dhanurvāṇānvita iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 139
pradyumno dakṣiṇe vajraṃ(1) śaṅkhaṃ vāme dhanuḥ kare //
49.d:
लाङ्गली मुषली रामो गदापद्मधरः स्मृतः /
:न्
1 वामोरुहृतदानव इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 गौराङ्गश्चायुधावृत इति ख, ग,
चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
3 धनुर्वाणान्वित इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 139
प्रद्युम्नो दक्षिणे वज्रं(1) शङ्खं वामे धनुः करे //
49.m:
Rāma is remembered holding a plough, pestle, mace, and lotus.
[...]
[Footnote 1: The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'vāmoruhṛtadānavaḥ'.]
[Footnote 2: The reading in the two manuscripts marked kha and ga is 'gaurāṅgaścāyudhāvṛtaḥ'.]
[Footnote 3: The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'dhanurvāṇānvitaḥ'.] / [Page 139]
Pradyumna holds a thunderbolt in his right hand, and a conch and bow in his left hand.

49.s:
gadānābhyāvṛtaḥ(2) pītyā pradyumno vā dhanuḥśarī /
caturbhujo niruddhaḥ syāttathā nārāyaṇo vibhuḥ //
49.d:
गदानाभ्यावृतः(2) पीत्या प्रद्युम्नो वा धनुःशरी /
चतुर्भुजो निरुद्धः स्यात्तथा नारायणो विभुः //
49.m:
Or Pradyumna holds a mace and lotus, accompanied by Rati, bearing bow and arrow.
Aniruddha should be four-armed, and likewise the all-pervading Nārāyaṇa.

49.s:
caturmukhaś caturbāhurvṛhajjaṭharamaṇḍalaḥ /
lambakūrco(3) jaṭāyukto vrahmā haṃsāgravāhanaḥ //
49.d:
चतुर्मुखश् चतुर्बाहुर्वृहज्जठरमण्डलः /
लम्बकूर्चो(3) जटायुक्तो व्रह्मा हंसाग्रवाहनः //
49.m:
Brahmā has four faces, four arms, a large belly,
a long beard, matted hair, and a swan-fronted vehicle.

49.s:
dakṣiṇe cākṣasūtrañca sruvo vāme tu kuṇḍikā /
ājyasthālī sarasvatī sāvitrī vāmadakṣiṇe //
49.d:
दक्षिणे चाक्षसूत्रञ्च स्रुवो वामे तु कुण्डिका /
आज्यस्थाली सरस्वती सावित्री वामदक्षिणे //
49.m:
In the right [hands] are a rosary and sacrificial ladle, and in the left a water-pot
and ghee-pot; Sarasvatī and Sāvitrī are on his left and right.

49.s:
viṣṇuraṣṭabhujastārkṣe kare khaḍgastu dakṣiṇe /
gadāśaraś ca varado vāme kārmukakheṭake //
49.d:
विष्णुरष्टभुजस्तार्क्षे करे खड्गस्तु दक्षिणे /
गदाशरश् च वरदो वामे कार्मुकखेटके //
49.m:
Viṣṇu has eight arms, mounted on Garuḍa; in the right hands are a sword,
mace, arrow, and boon-granting gesture; in the left are a bow and shield,

49.s:
cakraśaṅkhau caturbāhur narasiṃhaś caturbhujaḥ /
śaṅkhacakradharo vāpi vidāritamahāsuraḥ //
49.d:
चक्रशङ्खौ चतुर्बाहुर् नरसिंहश् चतुर्भुजः /
शङ्खचक्रधरो वापि विदारितमहासुरः //
49.m:
a discus, and a conch. Narasiṃha is four-armed,
or holding a conch and discus, having torn open the great demon.

49.s:
acaturbāhurvarāhastu śeṣaḥ pāṇitale dhṛtaḥ /
dhārayan bāhunā pṛthvīṃ vāmnena kamalādharaḥ(4) //
49.d:
अचतुर्बाहुर्वराहस्तु शेषः पाणितले धृतः /
धारयन् बाहुना पृथ्वीं वाम्नेन कमलाधरः(4) //
49.m:
Varāha has four arms, with Śeṣa held beneath his feet;
supporting the Earth with one arm, he holds a lotus with his left.

49.s:
pādalagnā dharā kāryā padā lakṣmīrvyavasthitā /
trailokyamohanastārkṣye aṣṭabāhustu dakṣiṇe //
49.d:
पादलग्ना धरा कार्या पदा लक्ष्मीर्व्यवस्थिता /
त्रैलोक्यमोहनस्तार्क्ष्ये अष्टबाहुस्तु दक्षिणे //
49.m:
Earth should be made clinging to his foot, while Lakṣmī is stationed at his foot.
Trailokyamohana is mounted on Garuḍa, with eight arms; in the right:

49.s:
cakraṃ khaḍgaṃ ca muṣalaṃ aṅkuśaṃ vāmake kare /
śaṅkhaśārṅgagadāpāśān padmavīṇāsamanvite //
49.d:
चक्रं खड्गं च मुषलं अङ्कुशं वामके करे /
शङ्खशार्ङ्गगदापाशान् पद्मवीणासमन्विते //
49.m:
a discus, sword, pestle, and goad; in the left hand:
a conch, bow, mace, and noose, accompanied by a lotus and lute.

49.s:
lakṣmīḥ sarasvatī kārye viśvarūpo 'tha dakṣiṇe /
mudgaraṃ ca tathā pāśaṃ śaktiśūlaṃ śaraṃ kare //
49.d:
लक्ष्मीः सरस्वती कार्ये विश्वरूपो ऽथ दक्षिणे /
मुद्गरं च तथा पाशं शक्तिशूलं शरं करे //
49.m:
Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī should be depicted. Now Viśvarūpa, on the right:
a club, noose, spear, trident, and arrow in hand;

49.s:
vāme śaṅkhañca śārṅgañca gadāṃ pāśaṃ ca tomaraṃ /
:n
1 dakṣiṇe cakramiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 gadī ratyāvṛta iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 lambabhruva iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭaḥ
4 dhārayannākulāṃ pṛthvīṃ vāmena kamalāmadha iti ṅa,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 140
lāṅgalaṃ paraśuṃ daṇḍaṃ churikāṃ carmakṣepakaṃ(1) //
49.d:
वामे शङ्खञ्च शार्ङ्गञ्च गदां पाशं च तोमरं /
:न्
1 दक्षिणे चक्रमिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 गदी रत्यावृत इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 लम्बभ्रुव इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाटः
4 धारयन्नाकुलां पृथ्वीं वामेन कमलामध इति ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 140
लाङ्गलं परशुं दण्डं छुरिकां चर्मक्षेपकं(1) //
49.m:
on the left, a conch, bow, mace, noose, and javelin;
[...]
[Footnote 1: The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'dakṣiṇe cakram'.]
[Footnote 2: The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'gadī ratyāvṛtaḥ'.]
[Footnote 3: The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'lambabhruvaḥ'.]
[Footnote 4: The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'dhārayannākulāṃ pṛthvīṃ vāmena kamalāmadhaḥ'.] / [Page 140]
a plough, axe, staff, dagger, and a shield-thrower.

49.s:
viṃśadbāhuś caturvaktro dakṣiṇasthotha vāmake /
trinetre vāmapārśve na śayito jalaśāyyapi //
49.d:
विंशद्बाहुश् चतुर्वक्त्रो दक्षिणस्थोथ वामके /
त्रिनेत्रे वामपार्श्वे न शयितो जलशाय्यपि //
49.m:
He has twenty arms and four faces, standing on the right or on the left;
or Jalaśāyin [Viṣṇu], three-eyed, reclining on his left side,

49.s:
śriyā dhṛtaikacaraṇo vimalādyābhirīḍitaḥ /
nābhipadmacaturvaktro hariśaṅkarako hariḥ //
49.d:
श्रिया धृतैकचरणो विमलाद्याभिरीडितः /
नाभिपद्मचतुर्वक्त्रो हरिशङ्करको हरिः //
49.m:
one foot held by Śrī, praised by Vimalā and others,
four-faced Brahmā in his navel-lotus, Hari as Hariśaṅkara.

49.s:
śūlarṣṭidhārī dakṣe ca gadācakradharo pade /
rudrakeśavalakṣmāṅgo gaurīlakṣmīsamanvitaḥ //
49.d:
शूलर्ष्टिधारी दक्षे च गदाचक्रधरो पदे /
रुद्रकेशवलक्ष्माङ्गो गौरीलक्ष्मीसमन्वितः //
49.m: Holding a trident and a spear on the right side, and bearing a mace and discus at his foot, / having the bodily characteristics of Rudra and Keśava, accompanied by Gaurī and Lakṣmī.

49.s:
śaṅkhacakragadāvedapāṇiścāśvaśirā hariḥ /
vāmapādo dhṛtaḥ śeṣe dakṣiṇaḥ kūrmapṛṣṭhagaḥ //
49.d:
शङ्खचक्रगदावेदपाणिश्चाश्वशिरा हरिः /
वामपादो धृतः शेषे दक्षिणः कूर्मपृष्ठगः //
49.m: Hari with the head of a horse has a conch, discus, mace, and the Vedas in his hands; / his left foot rests on Śeṣa, and the right rests on the back of a tortoise.

49.s:
dattātreyo dvibāhuḥ syādvāmotsaṅge śriyā saha /
viśvaksenaś cakragadī halī śaṅkhī harergaṇaḥ //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye pratimālakṣaṇaṃ nāma
ūnapañcāśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcāśodhyāyaḥ
devīpratimālakṣaṇakathanaṃ
49.d:
दत्तात्रेयो द्विबाहुः स्याद्वामोत्सङ्गे श्रिया सह /
विश्वक्सेनश् चक्रगदी हली शङ्खी हरेर्गणः //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये प्रतिमालक्षणं नाम
ऊनपञ्चाशो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चाशोध्यायः
देवीप्रतिमालक्षणकथनं
49.m:
Dattātreya should have two arms, with Śrī on his left lap. / Viśvaksena, an attendant of Hari, holds a discus, mace, ploughshare, and conch.
Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter, entitled “The Characteristics of Images,” in the venerable Agni Mahāpurāṇa.
Now, the fiftieth chapter.
The description of the characteristics of the images of the goddesses.

50.s:
bhagavānuvāca
caṇḍī viṃśatibāhuḥ syādbibhratī dakṣiṇaiḥ karaḥ /
śūlāsiśakticakrāṇi pāśaṃ kheṭāyudhābhayaṃ //
50.d:
भगवानुवाच
चण्डी विंशतिबाहुः स्याद्बिभ्रती दक्षिणैः करः /
शूलासिशक्तिचक्राणि पाशं खेटायुधाभयं //
50.m: The Lord said: / Caṇḍī should have twenty arms, holding with her right hands / a trident, sword, spear, discus, noose, shield, weapon, gesture of fearlessness,

50.s:
ḍamaruṃ śaktikāṃ vāmair nāgapāśañca kheṭakaṃ /
kuṭhāṅkuśacāpāṃś ca ghaṇṭādhvajagadāṃs tathā //
50.d:
डमरुं शक्तिकां वामैर् नागपाशञ्च खेटकं /
कुठाङ्कुशचापांश् च घण्टाध्वजगदांस् तथा //
50.m: a hand-drum, and a dart; with her left hands, a serpent-noose, a buckler, / an axe, an elephant-goad, a bow, a bell, a banner, a mace,

50.s:
ādarśamudgarān hastaiś caṇḍī vā daśabāhukā /
tadadho mahiṣaśchinnamūrdhā patitamastakaḥ //
:n
1 carma cottamamiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 141
50.d:
आदर्शमुद्गरान् हस्तैश् चण्डी वा दशबाहुका /
तदधो महिषश्छिन्नमूर्धा पतितमस्तकः //
:न्
1 चर्म चोत्तममिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 141
50.m:
a mirror, and a mallet; or Caṇḍī may have ten arms. / Beneath her is the buffalo with its head severed and fallen.
[Apparatus note]
1 “and an excellent hide” is the reading in manuscript ṅa. / [page 141]

50.s:
śastrodyatakaraḥ kruddhastadgrīvāsambhavaḥ pumān /
śūlahasto vamadrakto raktasraṅmūrdhajekṣaṇaḥ //
50.d:
शस्त्रोद्यतकरः क्रुद्धस्तद्ग्रीवासम्भवः पुमान् /
शूलहस्तो वमद्रक्तो रक्तस्रङ्मूर्धजेक्षणः //
50.m: Emerging from its neck is an enraged man with hand upraised with a weapon, / trident in hand, vomiting blood, with a blood-garland, [blood-red] hair and eyes,

50.s:
siṃhenāsvādyamānastu pāśabaddho gale bhṛśaṃ /
yāmyāṅghyrākrāntasiṃhā ca savyāṅghrirnīcagāsure //
50.d:
सिंहेनास्वाद्यमानस्तु पाशबद्धो गले भृशं /
याम्याङ्घ्य्राक्रान्तसिंहा च सव्याङ्घ्रिर्नीचगासुरे //
50.m: being savaged by the lion, tightly bound by a noose around the neck; / and she has her right foot resting upon the lion, and her left foot upon the fallen demon.

50.s:
caṇḍikeyaṃ trinetrā ca saśastrā ripumardanī /
navapadmātmake sthāne pūjyā durgā svamūrtitaḥ //
50.d:
चण्डिकेयं त्रिनेत्रा च सशस्त्रा रिपुमर्दनी /
नवपद्मात्मके स्थाने पूज्या दुर्गा स्वमूर्तितः //
50.m: This is Caṇḍikā, three-eyed, armed with weapons, the crusher of foes. / Durgā should be worshipped in a site of nine lotuses according to her icon,

50.s:
ādau madhye tathendrādau navātattvātmabhiḥ(1) kramāt /
aṣṭādaśabhujaikā tu dakṣe muṇḍaṃ ca kheṭakaṃ //
50.d:
आदौ मध्ये तथेन्द्रादौ नवातत्त्वात्मभिः(1) क्रमात् /
अष्टादशभुजैका तु दक्षे मुण्डं च खेटकं //
50.m: first in the center and then beginning with Indra[’s quarter], sequentially with the ninefold realities. / One has eighteen arms: on the right, a severed head, a shield,

50.s:
ādarśatarjanīcāpaṃ dhvajaṃ ḍamarukaṃ tathā /
pāśaṃ vāme bibhratī ca śaktimudgaraśūlakaṃ //
50.d:
आदर्शतर्जनीचापं ध्वजं डमरुकं तथा /
पाशं वामे बिभ्रती च शक्तिमुद्गरशूलकं //
50.m: a mirror, the warning gesture, a bow, a banner, a hand-drum, / and a noose; and holding in the left a dart, a mallet, a trident,

50.s:
vajrakhaḍgāṅkuśaśarān cakrandevī śalākayā /
etair evāyudhair yuktā śeṣāḥ ṣoḍaśabahukāḥ //
50.d:
वज्रखड्गाङ्कुशशरान् चक्रन्देवी शलाकया /
एतैर् एवायुधैर् युक्ता शेषाः षोडशबहुकाः //
50.m: a thunderbolt, sword, elephant-goad, arrows, and the discus, the goddess with a dart. / Endowed with these very weapons, the remaining [goddesses] have sixteen arms,

50.s:
ḍamaruṃ tarjanīṃ tyaktvā rudracaṇḍādayo nava /
rudracaṇḍā pracaṇḍā ca caṇḍogrā caṇḍanāyikā //
50.d:
डमरुं तर्जनीं त्यक्त्वा रुद्रचण्डादयो नव /
रुद्रचण्डा प्रचण्डा च चण्डोग्रा चण्डनायिका //
50.m: omitting the hand-drum and the warning gesture: the nine beginning with Rudracaṇḍā— / Rudracaṇḍā, Pracaṇḍā, Caṇḍogrā, Caṇḍanāyikā,

50.s:
caṇḍā caṇdavatī caiva caṇḍarūpāticaṇḍikā /
ugracaṇḍā ca madhyasthā rocanābhāruṇāsitā //
50.d:
चण्डा चण्दवती चैव चण्डरूपातिचण्डिका /
उग्रचण्डा च मध्यस्था रोचनाभारुणासिता //
50.m: Caṇḍā, Caṇḍavatī, Caṇḍarūpā, Aticaṇḍikā, / and Ugracaṇḍā situated in the center, possessing the radiance of yellow pigment, reddish, dark,

50.s:
nīlā śuklā dhūmrikā ca pītā śvetā ca siṃhagāḥ /
mahiṣotha pumān śastrī tatkacagrahamuṣṭikāḥ //
50.d:
नीला शुक्ला धूम्रिका च पीता श्वेता च सिंहगाः /
महिषोथ पुमान् शस्त्री तत्कचग्रहमुष्टिकाः //
50.m: blue, white, smoky, yellow, and white, mounted on lions; / then the buffalo and the man armed with weapons, with fists grasping their hair.

50.s:
ālīḍhā nava(2) durgāḥ syuḥ sthāpyāḥ putrādivṛddhaye /
tathā gaurī ca caṇḍikādyā kuṇḍyakṣararadāgnidhṛk //
50.d:
आलीढा नव(2) दुर्गाः स्युः स्थाप्याः पुत्रादिवृद्धये /
तथा गौरी च चण्डिकाद्या कुण्ड्यक्षररदाग्निधृक् //
50.m: The nine Durgās should be in the ālīḍha posture, installed for the increase of sons and the rest. / Likewise, Gaurī, beginning with Caṇḍikā, holds a water-pot, rosary, tooth, and fire.

50.s:
saiva rambhā vane siddhāgnihīnā lalitā tathā /
skandhamūrdhakarā vāme dvitīye dhṛtadarpaṇā //
:n
1 navatatvādibhirirti ṅa,cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 śālāsu nava iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 142
50.d:
सैव रम्भा वने सिद्धाग्निहीना ललिता तथा /
स्कन्धमूर्धकरा वामे द्वितीये धृतदर्पणा //
:न्
1 नवतत्वादिभिरिर्ति ङ,चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 शालासु नव इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 142
50.m:
She alone is Rambhā in the grove, having attained perfection without fire; likewise Lalitā / has her hands on her shoulder and head, holding a mirror in the second left [hand],
[Apparatus note]
1 “with the nine realities and the rest” is the reading in manuscript ṅa.
2 “nine in the halls” is the reading in manuscript ṅa. / [page 142]

50.s:
yāmye phalāñjalihastā saubhāgyā tatra cordhvikā /
lakṣmīryāmyakarāmbhojā vāme śrīphalasaṃyutā //
50.d:
याम्ये फलाञ्जलिहस्ता सौभाग्या तत्र चोर्ध्विका /
लक्ष्मीर्याम्यकराम्भोजा वामे श्रीफलसंयुता //
50.m: holding a cupped offering of fruit in the right hand; there, Saubhāgyā holds them raised aloft. / Lakṣmī has a lotus in her right hand and is endowed with a bilva fruit in the left.

50.s:
pustākṣamālikāhastā vīṇāhastā sarasvatī /
kumbhābjahastā śvetābhā makaropari jāhnavī (1)//
50.d:
पुस्ताक्षमालिकाहस्ता वीणाहस्ता सरस्वती /
कुम्भाब्जहस्ता श्वेताभा मकरोपरि जाह्नवी (1)//
50.m: Sarasvatī has a book and rosary in hand, and holds a vīṇā. / Jāhnavī is white-complexioned, with a pot and lotus in hand, upon a makara.

50.s:
kūrmagā yamunā kumbhakarā śyāmā ca pūjyate /
savīṇastumburuḥ śuklaḥ śūlī mātragrato vṛṣe //
50.d:
कूर्मगा यमुना कुम्भकरा श्यामा च पूज्यते /
सवीणस्तुम्बुरुः शुक्लः शूली मात्रग्रतो वृषे //
50.m: Yamunā, mounted on a tortoise, holding a pot, dark, is worshipped. / Tumburu, holding a vīṇā, white, trident-bearing, on a bull, stands before the mothers.

50.s:
gaurī caturmukhī brāhmī akṣamālāsurānvitā /
kuṇḍakṣapātriṇī vāme haṃsagā śāṅkarī sitā //
50.d:
गौरी चतुर्मुखी ब्राह्मी अक्षमालासुरान्विता /
कुण्डक्षपात्रिणी वामे हंसगा शाङ्करी सिता //
50.m: Gaurī is four-faced; Brāhmī is accompanied by a rosary and sacrificial ladle, / having a water-pot and ladle on the left, mounted on a goose; Śāṅkarī is white,

50.s:
śaracāpau dakṣiṇe 'syā vāme cakraṃ(2) dhanurvṛṣe /
kaumārī śikhigā raktā śaktihastā dvibāhukā //
50.d:
शरचापौ दक्षिणे ऽस्या वामे चक्रं(2) धनुर्वृषे /
कौमारी शिखिगा रक्ता शक्तिहस्ता द्विबाहुका //
50.m: having arrow and bow on her right, and on the left discus and bow, upon a bull. / Kaumārī is mounted on a peacock, red, holding a spear, two-armed.

50.s:
cakraśaṅkhadharā savye vāme lakṣmīrgadābjadhṛk /
daṇḍaśaṅkhāsi(3) gadayā vārāho mahiṣasthitā //
50.d:
चक्रशङ्खधरा सव्ये वामे लक्ष्मीर्गदाब्जधृक् /
दण्डशङ्खासि(3) गदया वाराहो महिषस्थिता //
50.m: Lakṣmī holds discus and conch on the right, and mace and lotus on the left. / Vārāhī stands upon a buffalo, with staff, conch, sword, and mace.

50.s:
aindrī vāme vajrahastā sahasrākṣī tu siddhaye /
cāmuṇḍā koṭarāghnī syānnirmāṃsā tu trilocanā //
50.d:
ऐन्द्री वामे वज्रहस्ता सहस्राक्षी तु सिद्धये /
चामुण्डा कोटराघ्नी स्यान्निर्मांसा तु त्रिलोचना //
50.m: Aindrī has a thunderbolt in her left hand, and is thousand-eyed for success. / Cāmuṇḍā should be hollow-eyed, emaciated, and three-eyed,

50.s:
nirmāṃsā asthisārā vā ūrdhvakeśī kṛśodarī /
dvīpacarmadharā vāme kapālaṃ paṭṭiśaṅkare //
50.d:
निर्मांसा अस्थिसारा वा ऊर्ध्वकेशी कृशोदरी /
द्वीपचर्मधरा वामे कपालं पट्टिशङ्करे //
50.m: fleshless or skeletal, hair standing upright, lean-bellied, / wearing a tiger skin, with a skull-bowl in the left hand and a paṭṭiśa weapon,

50.s:
śūlaṃ kartrī dakṣaṇe 'syāḥ śavārūḍhāsthitabhūṣaṇā /
vināyako narākāro vṛhatkukṣirgajānanaḥ //
50.d:
शूलं कर्त्री दक्षणे ऽस्याः शवारूढास्थितभूषणा /
विनायको नराकारो वृहत्कुक्षिर्गजाननः //
50.m: and with a trident and knife in her right, mounted on a corpse, adorned with bones. / Vināyaka has a human form, a large belly, and the face of an elephant,

50.s:
vṛhacchuṇḍo hy upavīto mukhaṃ saptakalaṃ bhavet /
vistārāddairghyatacaiva śuṇḍaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaṃ //
50.d:
वृहच्छुण्डो ह्य् उपवीतो मुखं सप्तकलं भवेत् /
विस्ताराद्दैर्घ्यतचैव शुण्डं षट्त्रिंशदङ्गुलं //
50.m: with a large trunk and wearing a sacred thread; his face should be seven kalās / in breadth and length, and the trunk thirty-six aṅgulas.

50.s:
kalā dvādaśa nāḍī tu grīvā sārdhakalocchritā /
ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaṃ kaṇṭhaṃ guhyamadhyardhamaṅgulaṃ //
:n
1 makareddhari jāhnavīti kha, gha, ṅa, cihnitapustatrayakapāṭhaḥ
2 vāme vajramiti kha, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
2 śaṅkhāri iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 143
50.d:
कला द्वादश नाडी तु ग्रीवा सार्धकलोच्छ्रिता /
षट्त्रिंशदङ्गुलं कण्ठं गुह्यमध्यर्धमङ्गुलं //
:न्
1 मकरेद्धरि जाह्नवीति ख, घ, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तत्रयकपाठः
2 वामे वज्रमिति ख, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
2 शङ्खारि इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 143
50.m:
The nāḍī is twelve kalās; the neck is one and a half kalās high; / the throat is thirty-six aṅgulas; the private parts are one and a half aṅgulas.
[Apparatus note]
1 “Jāhnavī upon a makara” is the reading in the three manuscripts kha, gha, and ṅa.
2 “a thunderbolt on the left” is the reading in the two manuscripts kha and ṅa.
3 “conch and discus” is the reading in manuscript kha. / [page 143]

50.s:
nābhirūrū dvādaśañca jaṅghe pāde tu dakṣiṇe /
svadantaṃ paraśuṃ vāme laḍḍukañcotpalaṃ śaye //
50.d:
नाभिरूरू द्वादशञ्च जङ्घे पादे तु दक्षिणे /
स्वदन्तं परशुं वामे लड्डुकञ्चोत्पलं शये //
50.m: The navel and thighs are twelve [aṅgulas], and the shanks and feet. In the right [hands] / [he holds] his own tusk and axe; in the left, a sweetmeat and blue lotus in the hand.

50.s:
sumukhī ca viḍālākṣī pārśve skando mayūragaḥ /
svāmī śākho viśākhaś ca dvibhujo bālarūpadhṛk //
50.d:
सुमुखी च विडालाक्षी पार्श्वे स्कन्दो मयूरगः /
स्वामी शाखो विशाखश् च द्विभुजो बालरूपधृक् //
50.m: Sumukhī and Viḍālākṣī are at his side. Skanda is mounted on a peacock, / as Svāmin, Śākha, and Viśākha, two-armed, bearing the form of a child,

50.s:
dakṣe śaktiḥ kukkuṭotha ekavaktrotha ṣaṇmukhaḥ /
ṣaḍbhujo vā dvādaśabhirgrāmeraṇye dvibāhukaḥ //
50.d:
दक्षे शक्तिः कुक्कुटोथ एकवक्त्रोथ षण्मुखः /
षड्भुजो वा द्वादशभिर्ग्रामेरण्ये द्विबाहुकः //
50.m: with a spear and rooster on the right, single-faced or six-faced, / six-armed, or with twelve [arms] in a village, or two-armed in the forest,

50.s:
śaktīṣupāśanistriṃśatotradostarjanīyutaḥ /
śaktyā dākṣiṇahasteṣu ṣaṭsu vāme kare tathā //
50.d:
शक्तीषुपाशनिस्त्रिंशतोत्रदोस्तर्जनीयुतः /
शक्त्या दाक्षिणहस्तेषु षट्सु वामे करे तथा //
50.m: endowed with a spear, arrow, noose, sword, goad, and the warning gesture, / with a spear among the six right hands; likewise in the left hands,

50.s:
śikhipicchandhanuḥ kheṭaṃ patākābhayakukkuṭe /
kapālakartarīśūlapāśabhṛdyāmyasaumyayoḥ //
50.d:
शिखिपिच्छन्धनुः खेटं पताकाभयकुक्कुटे /
कपालकर्तरीशूलपाशभृद्याम्यसौम्ययोः //
50.m: peacock feathers, a bow, shield, flag, fearlessness gesture, and a rooster. / Bearing a skull-bowl, scissors, trident, and noose in the right and left [hands],

50.s:
gajacarmabhṛdūrdhvāsyapādā syāt rudracarcikā /
saiva cāṣṭabhujā devī śiroḍamarukānvitā //
50.d:
गजचर्मभृदूर्ध्वास्यपादा स्यात् रुद्रचर्चिका /
सैव चाष्टभुजा देवी शिरोडमरुकान्विता //
50.m: wearing an elephant skin, with feet raised upward, Rudracarcikā should be. / That very goddess has eight arms, endowed with a severed head and hand-drum;

50.s:
tena sā rudracāmuṇḍā nāṭeśvaryatha nṛtyatī /
iyameva mahālakṣmīrupaviṣṭā caturmukhī //
50.d:
तेन सा रुद्रचामुण्डा नाटेश्वर्यथ नृत्यती /
इयमेव महालक्ष्मीरुपविष्टा चतुर्मुखी //
50.m: therefore she is Rudracāmuṇḍā; and as Nāṭeśvarī, she dances. / This very Mahālakṣmī is seated and four-faced,

50.s:
nṛvājimahiṣebhāṃś ca khādantī ca kare sthitān /
daśabāhustrinetrā ca śastrāsiḍamarutrikaṃ //
50.d:
नृवाजिमहिषेभांश् च खादन्ती च करे स्थितान् /
दशबाहुस्त्रिनेत्रा च शस्त्रासिडमरुत्रिकं //
50.m: devouring men, horses, buffaloes, and elephants held in her hands, / having ten arms, three eyes, holding a weapon, sword, and three hand-drums

50.s:
bibhratī dakṣiṇe haste vāme ghaṇṭāṃ ca kheṭakaṃ /
khaṭvāṅgaṃ ca triśūlañca siddhacāmuṇḍakāhvayā //
50.d:
बिभ्रती दक्षिणे हस्ते वामे घण्टां च खेटकं /
खट्वाङ्गं च त्रिशूलञ्च सिद्धचामुण्डकाह्वया //
50.m: in her right hands, and in the left a bell, shield, / khaṭvāṅga, and trident, named Siddhacāmuṇḍakā,

50.s:
siddhayogeśvarī devī sarvasiddhapradāyikā /
etadrūpā bhavedanyā pāśāṅkuśayutāruṇā //
50.d:
सिद्धयोगेश्वरी देवी सर्वसिद्धप्रदायिका /
एतद्रूपा भवेदन्या पाशाङ्कुशयुतारुणा //
50.m: the goddess Siddhayogeśvarī, granter of all perfections. / Another may be of this form, endowed with a noose and goad, reddish,

50.s:
bhairavī rūpavidyā tu bhujair dvādaśabhiryutā /
etāḥ śmaśānajā raudrā ambāṣṭakamidaṃ(1) smṛtaṃ //
:n
1 ādyāṣṭakamidamiti kha, ga, gha, cihnitapustakatrayapāṭhaḥ
:p 144
50.d:
भैरवी रूपविद्या तु भुजैर् द्वादशभिर्युता /
एताः श्मशानजा रौद्रा अम्बाष्टकमिदं(1) स्मृतं //
:न्
1 आद्याष्टकमिदमिति ख, ग, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकत्रयपाठः
:प् 144
50.m:
Bhairavī, having twelve arms, an embodiment of sacred knowledge. / These born in the cremation ground are fierce; this is remembered as the group of eight Mothers.
[Apparatus note]
1 “this original group of eight” is the reading in the three manuscripts kha, ga, and gha. / [page 144]

50.s:
kṣamā śivāvṛtā(1) vṛddhā dvibhujā vivṛtānanā /
danturā kṣemakarī syādbhūmau jānukarā sthitā //
50.d:
क्षमा शिवावृता(1) वृद्धा द्विभुजा विवृतानना /
दन्तुरा क्षेमकरी स्याद्भूमौ जानुकरा स्थिता //
50.m: Kṣamā is surrounded by jackals, aged, two-armed, with an open mouth, / protruding teeth, being Kṣemakarī, standing with hands upon her knees on the ground.

50.s:
yakṣiṇyastabdhadīrghākṣāḥ śākinyo vakradṛṣṭayaḥ(2) /
piṅgākṣāḥ syurmahāramyā rūpiṇyopsarasaḥ(3) sadā //
50.d:
यक्षिण्यस्तब्धदीर्घाक्षाः शाकिन्यो वक्रदृष्टयः(2) /
पिङ्गाक्षाः स्युर्महारम्या रूपिण्योप्सरसः(3) सदा //
50.m: The Yakṣiṇīs have fixed, long eyes; the Śākinīs have squinting eyes; / the Apsarases always have reddish-brown eyes, very charming, beautiful.

50.s:
sākṣamālī triśūlī ca nandīśo dvārapālakaḥ /
mahākālosimuṇḍī syācchūlakhaṭakavāṃs tathā //
50.d:
साक्षमाली त्रिशूली च नन्दीशो द्वारपालकः /
महाकालोसिमुण्डी स्याच्छूलखटकवांस् तथा //
50.m: Holding a rosary and a trident, Nandīśa is the door-keeper; / Mahākāla should have a sword and severed head, as well as a trident and club.

50.s:
kṛśo bhaṅgī ca nṛtyan vai kuṣmāṇḍasthūlakharvavān /
gajagokarṇavaktrādyā vīrabhadrādayo gaṇāḥ //
50.d:
कृशो भङ्गी च नृत्यन् वै कुष्माण्डस्थूलखर्ववान् /
गजगोकर्णवक्त्राद्या वीरभद्रादयो गणाः //
50.m: Bhṛṅgin is emaciated, bent, and dancing; the Kuṣmāṇḍa [gaṇas] are fat and dwarfish. / The gaṇas such as Vīrabhadra and others have faces resembling elephants, cows, ears, and so forth.

50.s:
ghaṇṭākarṇoṣṭadaśadoḥ pāparogaṃ vidārayan /
vajrāsidaṇḍacakreṣumuṣalāṅkuśamudgarān //
50.d:
घण्टाकर्णोष्टदशदोः पापरोगं विदारयन् /
वज्रासिदण्डचक्रेषुमुषलाङ्कुशमुद्गरान् //
50.m: Ghaṇṭākarṇa has eighteen arms, tearing apart sins and diseases; / [he holds] a thunderbolt, sword, staff, discus, arrow, pestle, elephant-goad, club,

50.s:
dakṣiṇe tarjanīṃ kheṭaṃ śaktiṃ muṇḍañca pāśakaṃ /
cāpaṃ ghaṇṭāṃ kuṭhārañca dvābhyāñcaiva triśūlakaṃ /
ghaṇṭāmālākulo devo visphoṭakavimardanaḥ(4) //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye devīpratimālakṣaṇaṃ nāma
pañcāśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha ekapañcāśo 'dhyāyaḥ
sūryādipratimālakṣaṇaṃ
50.d:
दक्षिणे तर्जनीं खेटं शक्तिं मुण्डञ्च पाशकं /
चापं घण्टां कुठारञ्च द्वाभ्याञ्चैव त्रिशूलकं /
घण्टामालाकुलो देवो विस्फोटकविमर्दनः(4) //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये देवीप्रतिमालक्षणं नाम
पञ्चाशो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ एकपञ्चाशो ऽध्यायः
सूर्यादिप्रतिमालक्षणं
50.m:
the index-finger gesture, shield, spear, severed head, noose, / bow, bell, and axe; and with two [hands he holds] a trident. / Bedecked with a garland of bells, the god crushes smallpox.
Thus ends the fiftieth chapter, named "Iconographic Characteristics of Goddesses," in the venerable Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
Now, the fifty-first chapter:
Iconographic Characteristics of Sūrya and Others.

51.s:
bhagavānuvāca
sasaptāśve saikacakre rathe sūryo dvipadmadhṛk /
masībhājanalekhanyau bibhratkuṇḍī tu dakṣiṇe //
51.d:
भगवानुवाच
ससप्ताश्वे सैकचक्रे रथे सूर्यो द्विपद्मधृक् /
मसीभाजनलेखन्यौ बिभ्रत्कुण्डी तु दक्षिणे //
51.m: The Lord said: / Sūrya is in a chariot with seven horses and a single wheel, holding two lotuses. / On the right [stands Piṅgala], bearing an inkpot, pen, and water-pot,

51.s:
vāme tu piṅgalo dvāri daṇḍabhṛt sa ravergaṇaḥ /
:n
1 śivācyuteti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 vajradṛṣṭaya iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 mahārathyo rūpiṇyo 'psarasa iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 visphoṭakaruṇardana iti ga, ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 145
bālavyajanadhāriṇyau pārśve rājñī ca niṣprabhā //
51.d:
वामे तु पिङ्गलो द्वारि दण्डभृत् स रवेर्गणः /
:न्
1 शिवाच्युतेति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 वज्रदृष्टय इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 महारथ्यो रूपिण्यो ऽप्सरस इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 विस्फोटकरुणर्दन इति ग, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 145
बालव्यजनधारिण्यौ पार्श्वे राज्ञी च निष्प्रभा //
51.m:
while on the left at the door is Daṇḍin holding a staff; these form the retinue of the Sun.
[...]
1. The reading in the manuscript marked kha is "śivācyuta".
2. The reading in the manuscript marked kha is "vajradṛṣṭayaḥ".
3. The reading in the manuscript marked kha is "mahārathyo rūpiṇyo 'psarasaḥ".
4. The reading in the manuscripts marked ga and ṅa is "visphoṭakaruṇardanaḥ".
On either side are Rājñī and Niṣprabhā holding flywhisks.

51.s:
athavāśvārūḍhaḥ kārya ekastu bhāskaraḥ /
varadā dvyabjanaḥ sarve dikpālāstrakarāḥ kramāt //
51.d:
अथवाश्वारूढः कार्य एकस्तु भास्करः /
वरदा द्व्यब्जनः सर्वे दिक्पालास्त्रकराः क्रमात् //
51.m: Or else, the solitary Sun should be depicted mounted on a horse. / All [deities] bestowing boons and holding two lotuses hold the weapons of the directional regents in order.

Those holding club, spear, discus, and lotus are stationed in the intermediate directions beginning with Agni. / On the twelve petals are the four-armed [forms] beginning with Sūrya and Aryaman, ending with [Mitra] and Rakṣas:

51.s:
varuṇaḥ sūryanāmā ca sahasrāṃśus tathāparaḥ /
dhātā tapanasañjñaś ca savitātha gabhastikaḥ //
51.d:
वरुणः सूर्यनामा च सहस्रांशुस् तथापरः /
धाता तपनसञ्ज्ञश् च सविताथ गभस्तिकः //
51.m: Varuṇa, the one named Sūrya, Sahasrāṃśu, and another; / Dhātṛ, the one designated Tapana, Savitṛ, and Gabhastin;

51.s:
raviś caivātha parjanyastvaṣṭā mitrotha viṣṇukaḥ /
meṣādirāśisaṃsthāś ca mārgādikārttikāntakāḥ //
51.d:
रविश् चैवाथ पर्जन्यस्त्वष्टा मित्रोथ विष्णुकः /
मेषादिराशिसंस्थाश् च मार्गादिकार्त्तिकान्तकाः //
51.m: Ravi, and Parjanya, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra, and Viṣṇu. / They reside in the zodiac signs beginning with Aries, and [govern the months] from Mārgaśīrṣa to Kārttika.

51.s:
kṛṣṇo rakto manāgraktaḥ pītaḥ pāṇḍarakaḥ sitaḥ /
kapilaḥ pītavarṇaś ca śukābho dhavalas tathā //
51.d:
कृष्णो रक्तो मनाग्रक्तः पीतः पाण्डरकः सितः /
कपिलः पीतवर्णश् च शुकाभो धवलस् तथा //
51.m: Black, red, slightly red, yellow, pale yellow, white, / tawny, golden-colored, parrot-hued, and bright white,

51.s:
dhūmro nīlaḥ kramādvarṇāḥ śaktayaḥ keśarāgragāḥ /
iḍā suṣumnā viśvārcirindusañjñā pramardinī(1) //
51.d:
धूम्रो नीलः क्रमाद्वर्णाः शक्तयः केशराग्रगाः /
इडा सुषुम्ना विश्वार्चिरिन्दुसञ्ज्ञा प्रमर्दिनी(1) //
51.m: smoky, and blue are their respective colors. The śaktis reside on the tips of the filaments: / Iḍā, Suṣumnā, Viśvārcis, the one designated Indu, Pramardinī,

51.s:
praharṣiṇī mahākālī kapilā ca prabodhanī /
nīlāmbarā ghanāntasthā amṛtākhyā ca śaktayaḥ //
51.d:
प्रहर्षिणी महाकाली कपिला च प्रबोधनी /
नीलाम्बरा घनान्तस्था अमृताख्या च शक्तयः //
51.m: Praharṣiṇī, Mahākālī, Kapilā, Prabodhanī, / Nīlāmbarā, Ghanāntasthā, and the śakti named Amṛtā.

51.s:
varuṇādeś ca tadvarṇāḥ keśarāgreṣu vinyaset /
tejaś caṇḍo mahāvakro(2) dvibhujaḥ padmakhadgabhṛt(3) //
51.d:
वरुणादेश् च तद्वर्णाः केशराग्रेषु विन्यसेत् /
तेजश् चण्डो महावक्रो(2) द्विभुजः पद्मखद्गभृत्(3) //
51.m: One should deposit them on the tips of the filaments according to their colors from Varuṇa onwards. / Tejas, Caṇḍa, and Mahāvakro are two-armed, holding a lotus and a sword.

51.s:
kuṇḍikājapyāmālīnduḥ kujaḥ śaktyakṣamālikaḥ /
budhaścāpākṣapāṇiḥ syājjīvaḥ kuṇḍyakṣamālikaḥ //
:n
1 viśvācī vindusañjñāpravardhanī iti ṅa,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 mahārakta iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ / mārtaṇḍaś ca mahārakta
iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 padmakhaḍgadhṛgiti ga, gha, cihnitapustakapustakapāṭhaḥ /
khaḍgacarmabhṛditi ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 146
51.d:
कुण्डिकाजप्यामालीन्दुः कुजः शक्त्यक्षमालिकः /
बुधश्चापाक्षपाणिः स्याज्जीवः कुण्ड्यक्षमालिकः //
:न्
1 विश्वाची विन्दुसञ्ज्ञाप्रवर्धनी इति ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 महारक्त इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः / मार्तण्डश् च महारक्त
इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 पद्मखड्गधृगिति ग, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपुस्तकपाठः /
खड्गचर्मभृदिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 146
51.m:
The Moon holds a water-pot and a rosary; Mars holds a spear and a rosary; / Mercury holds a bow and a rosary; Jupiter holds a water-pot and a rosary;
[...]
1. The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is "viśvācī vindusañjñāpravardhanī".
2. The reading in the manuscript marked kha is "mahāraktaḥ"; the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is "mārtaṇḍaś ca mahāraktaḥ".
3. The reading in the manuscripts marked ga and gha is "padmakhaḍgadhṛk".
The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is "khaḍgacarmabhṛt".

51.s:
śukraḥ kuṇḍyakṣamālī syāt kiṇkiṇīsūtravāñchaniḥ(1) /
ardhacandradharo rāhuḥ ketuḥ khaḍgī ca dīpabhṛt //
51.d:
शुक्रः कुण्ड्यक्षमाली स्यात् किण्किणीसूत्रवाञ्छनिः(1) /
अर्धचन्द्रधरो राहुः केतुः खड्गी च दीपभृत् //
51.m: Venus holds a water-pot and a rosary; Saturn holds a girdle of small bells. / Rāhu holds a crescent moon; and Ketu bears a sword and a lamp.

51.s:
anantastakṣakaḥ karkaḥ padmo mahābjaḥ śaṅkhakaḥ /
kulikaḥ sūtriṇaḥ sarve phaṇavaktrā mahāprabhāḥ //
51.d:
अनन्तस्तक्षकः कर्कः पद्मो महाब्जः शङ्खकः /
कुलिकः सूत्रिणः सर्वे फणवक्त्रा महाप्रभाः //
51.m: Ananta, Takṣaka, Karkakoṭaka, Padma, Mahāpadma, Śaṅkha, / and Kulika all wear sacred threads, have hood-bearing faces, and possess great radiance.

51.s:
indro vajrī gajārūḍhaśchāgagogniś ca śaktimān /
yamo daṇḍī ca mahiṣe nairṛtaḥ khaḍgavān kare //
51.d:
इन्द्रो वज्री गजारूढश्छागगोग्निश् च शक्तिमान् /
यमो दण्डी च महिषे नैरृतः खड्गवान् करे //
51.m: Indra bears a thunderbolt and is mounted on an elephant; Agni is on a goat and bears a spear; / Yama carries a staff on a buffalo; Nirṛti holds a sword in his hand;

51.s:
makare varuṇaḥ pāśī vāyurdhvajadharo mṛge /
gadī(2) kuvero meṣastha īśānaś ca jaṭī vṛṣe //
51.d:
मकरे वरुणः पाशी वायुर्ध्वजधरो मृगे /
गदी(2) कुवेरो मेषस्थ ईशानश् च जटी वृषे //
51.m: Varuṇa carries a noose on a makara; Vāyu holds a banner on a deer; / Kubera carries a club and sits on a ram; and Īśāna, with matted hair, sits on a bull.

51.s:
dvibāhavo lokapālā viśvakarmākṣasūtrabhṛt /
hanūmān vajrahastaḥ syāt padbhyāṃ sampīḍitāśrayaḥ //
51.d:
द्विबाहवो लोकपाला विश्वकर्माक्षसूत्रभृत् /
हनूमान् वज्रहस्तः स्यात् पद्भ्यां सम्पीडिताश्रयः //
51.m: The world-guardians have two arms. Viśvakarman carries a rosary. / Hanūmat has a thunderbolt in his hand, his support pressed firmly by both feet.

51.s:
vīṇāhastāḥ kinnarāḥ syurmālāvidyādharāś ca khe(3) /
durbalāṅgāḥ piśācāḥ syurvetālā vikṛtānanāḥ(4) /
kṣetrapālāḥ śūlavantaḥ(5) pretā mahodarāḥ kṛśāḥ //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye pratimālakṣaṇaṃ nāma ekapañcāśo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha dvipañcośo 'dhyāyaḥ
devīpratimālakṣaṇaṃ
51.d:
वीणाहस्ताः किन्नराः स्युर्मालाविद्याधराश् च खे(3) /
दुर्बलाङ्गाः पिशाचाः स्युर्वेताला विकृताननाः(4) /
क्षेत्रपालाः शूलवन्तः(5) प्रेता महोदराः कृशाः //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये प्रतिमालक्षणं नाम एकपञ्चाशो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ द्विपञ्चोशो ऽध्यायः
देवीप्रतिमालक्षणं
51.m:
